title: OPERATION CRANE WARD
situation: {WORLD} is safe for now because the invaders won it by a formal challenge, and their own honor code stops them from simply taking it back. A batchall is that challenge: a Clan names the force it will bring and the prize it wants, and both sides fight to the terms. When the {TARGET_FACTION} lost their batchall here in {YEAR}, they gave up the world. {EMPLOYER} now uses it as a workshop. The test sheds in {DISTRICT} rebuild captured Clan machines and test new designs {EMPLOYER} will field on the next world. The {TARGET_FACTION} cannot retake {WORLD} without shaming their Khan's word. But a single Star Colonel can still call a Trial of Possession for a named asset, and they do. {EMPLOYER} has assigned your {FORCE_SIZE} to hold {DISTRICT} through the monsoon quarter. The ground both helps and hurts you. The causeway is the only hard-surface route between the landing flats and the test sheds: a raised ferrocrete road 38 kilometers long and 22 meters wide, strong enough for the heaviest 'Mechs. Everything off the causeway is flooded rice terraces for the whole monsoon quarter. 'Mechs of 55 tons and under cross the paddies at half speed. Heavier machines sink to the hip within 90 meters and must be winched out. When a monsoon cell is overhead, you can see only {monsoonVisibility} meters and thermal sensors lose another 30 percent. Your contact {NPC:intel-source} intercepted a {TARGET_FACTION} bid list naming the sheds as a target. That intercept is 9 days old, so treat it as likely but not certain. It projects a force of {jaguarTrialMechs} OmniMechs and {jaguarElementalPoints} Points of Elementals — armored infantry, five troopers to a Point — under {NPC:opfor-commander}. His record shows two past Trials fought strictly by the dueling code, and one batchall he abandoned in disgust when militia used inferno rockets against him. Honor is a trap for both sides here. The Coordinator's order is blunt: this world matters because it proves the Clans can be beaten by a fair fight. Win by drowning the {TARGET_FACTION} in mud and you keep the sheds but throw away that proof. Lose the sheds and you lose both. The clock is the convoy. The quarter's prototype shipment — {convoyVehicles} sealed transporters — starts crossing the causeway to the hardened bunkers 24 hours after the {TARGET_FACTION} land. It cannot wait: the flood closes the bunker road right behind it.

objectives.primary: Hold the test sheds and get the prototype shipment into the bunkers undamaged by T+27:10.
objectives.secondary: End the fight as a formal challenge fought to its stated terms, so {EMPLOYER} can point to it as a fair win or a fair loss — either way, not a mud-brawl.
objectives.bonus: Disable, do not destroy, at least 1 {TARGET_FACTION} OmniMech inside the agreed dueling ground, so it can be captured and studied.

complications.name: Monsoon Cell Rotation
complications.text: Storm cells cross the floodlands on a 4-hour cycle and sit overhead for roughly 70 minutes at a time. Under a cell, the paddies and the causeway are equally blind, and VTOL support cannot fly.
complications.mechanicalEffect: While a cell is overhead: maximum sensor and visual range equals {monsoonVisibility} meters, no aerial reconnaissance, and indirect fire requires a forward spotter with line of sight.

complications.name: The Rigged Causeway Spans
complications.text: During the panic of 3050, engineers wired demolition charges into causeway spans 9 and 23 and never removed them. Blowing a span blocks heavy crossings both ways for the whole season. It also destroys state property. Do that without district approval and the ISF — the employer's secret police — opens a file that outlasts the battle.
complications.mechanicalEffect: To blow a span you need approval: spend one full turn at the command post, then wait 2 turns for the answer. The commander can blow it on his own authority instead — but that forces the COMPROMISED outcome at mission end, no matter how the fight goes.

complications.name: Paddy Labor Levy
complications.text: 1,400 civilian workers are on harvest levy along the south terraces and cannot be cleared in under 12 hours. {TARGET_FACTION} warriors will not deliberately target them, but stray fire that kills levy workers hands {TARGET_FACTION} a grievance claim and the prefecture a scandal.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each incident of stray-fire civilian casualties voids the bonus objective's salvage rights and adds one cumulative penalty step to the post-mission settlement.

complications.name: Elemental Dike Infiltration
complications.text: {TARGET_FACTION} Elementals can move along the irrigation dikes submerged to the shoulders, and sensor returns read them as livestock until 120 meters. The dike network reaches within 800 meters of the sheds.
complications.mechanicalEffect: {TARGET_FACTION} Elemental Points may deploy under hidden-unit rules in any hex within 4 hexes of a dike hex.

decisionPoints.name: The Answer to the Batchall
decisionPoints.context: {NPC:opfor-commander} declares a Trial of Possession for the test sheds and proposes the engagement circle on the causeway itself, spans 12 through 19 — hard, open ferrocrete, forces as bid. The reply window is 2 hours. District command has, deliberately, left the answer to the garrison commander.

options.title: Accept the Circle
advantages: Zellbrigen caps the numbers you face at the declared bid
Hard ground lets your assault machines fight at full mobility
A clean win on their terms is the exact legend {WORLD} exists to produce
disadvantages: OmniMech for 'Mech, their machines outrange and outgun yours on open ferrocrete
No terrain assistance, no minefields, no militia support inside the circle
options.consequence: The Trial is fought as a set of one-on-one duels on the causeway. The result is clear and public, and the {TARGET_FACTION} honor it for the season.

costs.resource: given up inside the dueling ground: minefields, militia support, and the floodland advantage
costs.risk: duels on open ferrocrete against OmniMechs that outrange you. If the Trial runs its full course, expect 1,200,000 to 1,800,000 C-bills in armor and actuator repairs.

options.title: Counter-Bid the Ground
advantages: Paddy mud negates their tonnage advantage and your pilots drilled the terraces all season
Monsoon cells shorten engagement ranges to where your refits trade evenly
disadvantages: {NPC:opfor-commander} may read the counter-bid as cowardice and add more forces in reply
In a storm cell, the duel can fall apart into a blind melee no referee can score — so you lose control of the honor result
options.consequence: If the {TARGET_FACTION} accept, the Trial is fought in the floodlands during the monsoon. If they refuse, they land with the reserve forces their first bid had held back.

costs.resource: winch-recovery teams and tow gear staged at the paddy edges to pull out bogged machines all season
costs.risk: if the counter-bid reads as cowardice, {NPC:opfor-commander} adds more forces; in a storm cell the honor result slips out of your control

options.title: Refuse the Trial
advantages: Every weapon becomes lawful: mines, infernos, militia, pre-registered artillery
Highest raw probability of keeping the sheds intact this quarter
disadvantages: Trades away why this world matters — proof the Clans can be beaten fairly — just to save the equipment in it
The {TARGET_FACTION} are freed from the dueling code: expect them to gang fire, and no formal challenge next time
The ISF will want to know who decided {EMPLOYER} is afraid of a duel
options.consequence: The fight becomes open war in the floodlands. Win or lose, the next {TARGET_FACTION} attack on {WORLD} comes with no warning and no challenge.

costs.resource: the reason this world matters — proof the Clans can be beaten fairly — spent to save the equipment
costs.risk: the ISF opens a file on who decided {EMPLOYER} fears a duel; the {TARGET_FACTION} are freed from the dueling code for the season

entries.event: Batchall received; {TARGET_FACTION} DropShips announce descent toward the landing flats.
First DropShip lands. The Trial force unloads under the bid's truce; neither side may fire.
Reply window closes. Silence counts as refusing the Trial.
Earliest {TARGET_FACTION} movement to the agreed circle (acceptance) or to assault positions (refusal).
Prototype convoy departs the sheds for the bunkers. It cannot be recalled once rolling.
Convoy scheduled inside the bunkers; bunker doors seal for the flood season.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The consignment is exposed on the causeway from T+24:00 to T+27:10 and the schedule does not move. If any {TARGET_FACTION} unit holds a causeway span at T+24:00, the consignment — and the quarter's work — is forfeit.

opforSketch.composition: Trial-bid OmniMech force at the top of the band in quality, not quantity: front-line {TARGET_FACTION} OmniMechs in a heavy-leaning mix (1 to 1.5 Stars across the threat band) with 1-3 Points of Elementals. No armor, no artillery, no aerospace inside the bid. If zellbrigen is broken, a Trinary-equivalent reserve becomes available to {TARGET_FACTION} at +48 hours.
opforSketch.behavior: Rigid zellbrigen until provoked: single-target engagements, withdrawal honored, no physical attacks. Any break of honor converts the force to concentrated-fire doctrine with Elemental headhunting against the garrison command 'Mech.

forks.name: OPERATION LONG HARVEST
forks.trigger: The Trial is won inside its declared terms and the consignment reaches the bunkers.
forks.consequence: District command authorizes a baited repeat: the next consignment is quietly advertised, and the garrison prepares a formal defense with a full season of preparation — under the eyes of a visiting {EMPLOYER} evaluation board.

forks.name: OPERATION GLEANING
forks.trigger: The {TARGET_FACTION} take the sheds or the convoy.
forks.consequence: The captured prototypes are staged at the landing flats for lift within 72 hours. A scratch force must destroy what {EMPLOYER} cannot recover before the DropShips burn.

forks.name: OPERATION QUIET COURT
forks.trigger: The garrison won by refusing the batchall or by dropping a causeway span without authorization.
forks.consequence: The ISF convenes an inquiry on {WORLD}. The unit holds the district through 30 days of {TARGET_FACTION} honor-raids arriving without declaration while its officers testify, one at a time.

storyElementSeed: Between monsoon cells, a maintenance crew sweeps standing water off the causeway deck with long rubber blades ahead of the convoy rehearsal, pausing to let a farm cart pass between the legs of a parked assault 'Mech.

phases.name: THE BATCHALL
phases.lead: The declaration arrives with the {TARGET_FACTION} descent, and the 2-hour reply window belongs to the garrison commander alone. District command has withheld its guidance deliberately; the answer given will be read at the capital either way.

dataBlock.Reply Window: 2 hours from receipt; silence counts as refusing the Trial
dataBlock.Bid Truce: Neither side may fire while the Trial force unloads at the landing flats
dataBlock.Intercepted Bid List: {jaguarTrialMechs} OmniMechs and {jaguarElementalPoints} Points of Elementals; the intercept is 9 days old, so treat it as likely, not confirmed
dataBlock.Proposed Dueling Ground: Causeway spans 12 through 19 — 8 spans of open ferrocrete, 22 meters wide

sidebarKernel.kernel: The bid list is 9 days old, and {NPC:opfor-commander} once walked away from a batchall in disgust. The list tells you what he planned to bring. It does not tell you what anger will make him bring.

phases.name: THE TRIAL
phases.lead: You fight on whichever ground your answer chose: the ferrocrete dueling ground or the flooded terraces. Monsoon cells roll through on their own schedule and spare no one. Hold to the stated terms exactly, because {EMPLOYER} will publish whatever happens here.

dataBlock.Monsoon Cell Cycle: 4-hour rotation, approximately 70 minutes overhead per cell
dataBlock.Visibility Under Cell: {monsoonVisibility} meters; thermal degraded a further 30 percent; no VTOL flight
dataBlock.Paddy Bogging: 55 tons and under cross at half speed; heavier machines bog to the hip within 90 meters
dataBlock.Winch Recovery: Staged at the paddy margins — one bogged assault 'Mech requires 2 recovery vehicles and 40 minutes

sidebarKernel.kernel: The first exchange of fire decides whether the duel holds. One inferno volley from militia in the terraces ends the dueling code for the season, and command will be blamed as if it gave the order.

phases.name: THE CAUSEWAY RUN
phases.lead: From T+24:00 the shipment is on the causeway, and the mission comes down to a 38-kilometer run against the clock. Whatever survived the Trial escorts {convoyVehicles} transporters down a road with no exits and no backup schedule.

dataBlock.Convoy Exposure: T+24:00 to T+27:10 — 3 hours 10 minutes on elevated ferrocrete, no concealment
dataBlock.Causeway Rating: 22 meters wide, assault-class traffic, spans numbered 1 through 41
dataBlock.Charged Spans: 9 and 23 — demolition charges laid in the invasion panic of 3050, never lifted
dataBlock.Bunker Seal: the bunker doors close at T+27:10 for the flood season; the schedule does not move

phases.protocol: Blowing a span needs district approval. Send the request from the command post — that costs one full turn — and the answer comes 2 turns later. Either way, the ISF logs who signed off. The commander can blow a span on his own authority, but that triggers the COMPROMISED outcome; weigh that before ordering it. The convoy escort reports in at every fifth span on the engineering net. Two missed reports in a row halt the whole column.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The transporters are sealed and the manifests are not the garrison's to read — plan the escort around their weight class and turning radius, which the yardmaster will provide, and ask nothing else.

merc.objectives.primary: Hold the sheds and get the shipment into the bunkers by T+27:10. The contract pays if you hold the ground at the deadline, not for fighting pretty. The honor clauses are the employer's worry — until he adds them to your bond.

clan.objectives.secondary: Conclude the Trial within zellbrigen. A victory of mud and mines is not a victory; it is a confession.

resourceGates.lackingText: No district depot allotment on hand: mine, inferno, and artillery stocks come through {EMPLOYER} quartermaster channels at 610,000 C-bills, ISF countersignature required.

title: OPERATION COLD LEDGER
situation: {WORLD} sits one jump from the {TARGET_FACTION} occupation zone. That makes it dangerous, and the garrison contract pays a border bonus to match. {EMPLOYER} hired your {FORCE_SIZE} to hold the fjord settlements: the spaceport, the molybdenum works, and 19,000 civilians spread along 60 kilometers of frozen coast. The key term is clause 7(c) — defend only. Fire first across the truce line and you lose your damage coverage and hand the employer grounds to fire you. The {TARGET_FACTION} understand this contract's fine print better than the employer's own lawyers, and they will use it. Your terrain problem is the ice road. From the first hard freeze to the spring melt, the only route between the spaceport and the works is 31 kilometers of plowed lake ice. Engineers rate it for 60 tons standing still and 45 tons moving. Anything heavier breaks through, and the lake is 80 meters deep. Your heavy 'Mechs can defend one end or the other, not both — unless they take the shoulder trail, a single-file detour that costs 9 hours. At -40 degrees your machines shed heat easily, but exposed joints freeze between fights and exposed infantry die in 40 minutes. Two weeks ago a {TARGET_FACTION} fighter flew over the spaceport at 400 meters in clear daylight, weapon racks empty. That was a message, not a scouting run. Then 4 days ago {NPC:intel-source} passed something worse: a {TARGET_FACTION} Star Captain has filed a Trial of Possession — a formal challenge — for your own Clan salvage. That salvage is 2 OmniMech hulls you recovered legally under last contract's salvage clause and stored in the works. This item is only 4 days old but not fully confirmed, so plan on it. The employer's liaison has said it plainly: the salvage is yours, the world is theirs, and if the {TARGET_FACTION} come for your property he would rather the fight not happen at the spaceport, the works, or the ice road that feeds 19,000 people. Nobody is paying extra for that preference. The {TARGET_FACTION} challenge, if it comes, arrives on its own schedule. The ice road closes when the thaw arrives — forecast 11 to 18 days out. Your books have to survive both.

objectives.primary: Hold the spaceport, the works, and your stored salvage through the contract period without breaking clause 7(c).
objectives.secondary: Keep the ice road open until the official thaw closure — no spans dropped, no wrecks blocking the route.
objectives.bonus: Settle any {TARGET_FACTION} challenge in a way the employer can call a lawful, defensive action, so the border bonus survives into the next contract.

complications.name: Clause 7(c)
complications.text: Defend only. If your unit clearly fires first across the truce line, you lose your damage coverage and the employer can fire you for cause. The {TARGET_FACTION} have seen this kind of contract before and will maneuver in close to bait you into shooting first.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If any of your 'Mechs fires before a {TARGET_FACTION} unit fires in that fight, you pay all repair and salvage costs for the mission yourself, and the mission ends on the COMPROMISED outcome.

complications.name: The Ice Road Limit
complications.text: The lake route is rated 60 tons static, 45 tons moving. A breakthrough does not just kill the machine — it closes the route and cuts the works' food resupply to airlift only.
complications.mechanicalEffect: 'Mechs over 45 tons crossing at above walking speed, or over 60 tons at any speed, roll for ice failure each turn on the route; a failure removes the unit from the battle and closes the road for the scenario and all forks.

complications.name: Deep Cold
complications.text: Ambient -40 degrees, wind off the fjord. Heat dissipation is excellent until intake icing sets in during lulls.
complications.mechanicalEffect: All units dissipate +2 heat per turn; any 'Mech that spends 3 consecutive turns without firing or running takes an actuator-icing critical check on first movement. Conventional infantry cannot deploy outside vehicles or structures for more than 4 turns.

complications.name: The Liaison's Preference
complications.text: {NPC:employer-contact} wants any fight moved away from civilian infrastructure and will not put that in writing. Compliance is unpaid; refusal is remembered at renewal.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each objective structure (spaceport, works, road) that takes incidental damage applies a penalty step at contract settlement, separate from combat results.

decisionPoints.name: The Salvage Question
decisionPoints.context: The batchall arrives: a {TARGET_FACTION} Star Captain declares a Trial of Possession for the 2 stored OmniMech chassis, bidding a Star of OmniMechs, and proposes the frozen marsh flats north of the works as the circle. Reply window 72 hours. The employer's counsel observes, unhelpfully, that answering a trial about your own property is probably not a 7(c) violation.

options.title: Meet the Trial
advantages: {TARGET_FACTION} honor caps the engagement at the bid — the cheapest fight on offer
Winning before witnesses raises the unit's rating with Clan and Inner Sphere employers alike
The circle is away from all three objective structures, which is exactly what the liaison wants
disadvantages: A Star of front-line {TARGET_FACTION} OmniMechs is a brutal fight for any lance you can pull off garrison duty
Losses in a fight you chose may be ruled outside your damage coverage
options.consequence: The trial is fought as bid on the marsh flats. Win or lose, {TARGET_FACTION} honor the result and the garrison period continues — minus whatever the fight cost.

costs.resource: one lance off the garrison posts for the trial — the spaceport or the works stands thin, and the shoulder trail swap is 9 hours
costs.risk: losses in a voluntary engagement may be argued outside loss-and-damage coverage — own-cost repairs against a front-line {TARGET_FACTION} Star

options.title: Refuse and Fortify
advantages: Forces {TARGET_FACTION} to choose between dropping the claim and a truce-violating attack on a defended works
Every defensive asset — mines, hull-down positions, the works' walls — is in play if they come anyway
disadvantages: If they come anyway, the fight happens at the works, among the buildings you must protect and the civilians
Refusing looks dishonorable to them — dezgra — so expect them to bring everything and give no warning next time
options.consequence: The {TARGET_FACTION} either withdraw the claim, with contempt, or attack the works unbid within 8 days — a HIGH-threat engagement on the worst possible ground.

costs.resource: mine stocks and barrier works emplaced at the perimeter
costs.risk: an unbid {TARGET_FACTION} attack inside 8 days lands among the objective structures — every structure hit is a penalty step at settlement

options.title: Sell the Claim
advantages: Handing over 2 unrestorable chassis ends the threat at zero combat cost
The thaw deadline and the road stay unthreatened; the contract period closes quietly
disadvantages: The salvage is the unit's only hard asset from the last contract — that is next year's refit budget
Word travels: a unit that yields property on demand invites the next demand
The employer notes that {TARGET_FACTION} now believe pressure works on this garrison
options.consequence: The chassis leave on a {TARGET_FACTION} DropShip under truce protocol. The unit's ledger takes the loss, the garrison period continues, and the next {TARGET_FACTION} message will be priced accordingly.

costs.resource: the 2 Clan OmniMech chassis — the unit's only hard asset from the last contract and next year's refit budget
costs.risk: word travels: a unit that yields property on demand invites the next demand

entries.event: {TARGET_FACTION} DropShip burn flagged inbound by the spaceport sensor net; batchall transmitted simultaneously.
Garrison stand-to complete; lances committed to either the spaceport or the works cannot swap ends in under 9 hours via the shoulder trail.
Projected {TARGET_FACTION} grounding on the marsh flats if the trial is accepted.
Batchall reply window closes. Silence is refusal.
Latest projected unbid {TARGET_FACTION} action if refused.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The thaw closes the ice road on its own schedule — forecast 11 to 18 days out, {thawDay} days in actuality. After closure, the works and its garrison detachment are supplied by air only, and any fight there is fought with whatever was positioned before the melt. Position before the thaw or accept being split.

opforSketch.composition: One Star of front-line {TARGET_FACTION} OmniMechs at the band's quality ceiling, medium-heavy mix built for mobility on ice and marsh; 1 Point of Elementals riding as trial witnesses and perimeter security. If the trial is refused and {TARGET_FACTION} attack unbid, add a second Star and an aerospace point at +8 days.
opforSketch.behavior: Patient and legalistic: {TARGET_FACTION} maneuver to provoke a first shot near the truce line, honor zellbrigen scrupulously inside a declared trial, and fight with massed efficiency the moment the engagement is unbid. They will not deliberately damage civilian infrastructure — and will note for the record every time you do.

forks.name: OPERATION GOOD PAPER
forks.trigger: All three structures intact, salvage retained, no 7(c) breach.
forks.consequence: The employer exercises the renewal option at an improved multiplier and asks the unit to host a {EMPLOYER} intelligence team running close observation of the {TARGET_FACTION} border — quiet work that makes the garrison a collection target.

forks.name: OPERATION THAW DEBT
forks.trigger: The salvage is lost by force, or an objective structure is destroyed.
forks.consequence: The contract settles at penalty rates and the unit must take an immediate follow-on job — escorting the spring resupply convoy up the just-opened fjord road through ground {TARGET_FACTION} now patrol at leisure.

forks.name: OPERATION PAPER STORM
forks.trigger: Clause 7(c) was breached or argued breached.
forks.consequence: Coverage is suspended pending arbitration. The unit fights the remainder of the garrison period at own-cost repairs while the employer's lawyers and the unit's bondholder fight a colder war than {TARGET_FACTION} ever offered.

storyElementSeed: At the ice road checkpoint, a tech with a paint scraper works frost off a 'Mech's knee actuator while two drivers from the food convoy argue quietly about whether the lake creaked or the wind did.

phases.name: POSTURE
phases.lead: This garrison is a placement problem: two strongpoints, one ice road, and heavy 'Mechs that can hold one end or the other but not both. Whatever you position in the first week is what fights in the last, because swapping ends costs 9 hours and the thaw is already on the calendar.

routes.name: ICE ROAD
routes.desc: 31 kilometers of plowed lake ice between the spaceport and the works, rated 60 tons static, 45 tons moving.
routes.tradeoff: Fast for anything under the rating; a breakthrough closes the road for the season and puts the works on airlift rations.

routes.name: THE SHOULDER
routes.desc: 9-hour detour over the fjord shoulder, single-file, all weights.
routes.tradeoff: The only route for heavies — and 9 hours is longer than any fight either town is likely to host.

dataBlock.Posting Split: Spaceport, molybdenum works, 19,000 civilians across 60 kilometers of coastline
dataBlock.Cold Exposure: -40 degrees ambient; exposed infantry dies in 40 minutes; actuators ice during engagement lulls
dataBlock.End-Swap Time: 9 hours via the shoulder for anything over the ice rating

sidebarKernel.kernel: Every machine that sits picket gets an icing schedule taped inside the cockpit: 3 turns idle is a frozen actuator, and {TARGET_FACTION} can read a cold-start limp at 2 kilometers.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT
phases.lead: The challenge, if it comes, is as much a legal trap as a fight — the {TARGET_FACTION} wrote it so that every answer costs you something. You get 72 hours to reply, which is just long enough for the employer's lawyers to be no help at all.
phases.protocol: Clause 7(c) fire discipline: no 'Mech fires until a {TARGET_FACTION} weapon shows on your gun-camera. Log every contact with a timestamp and its position against the truce line. Within 6 hours of any exchange, the duty officer sends the full log to the employer's liaison. That recording is your insurance — guard it as carefully as ammunition.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The {TARGET_FACTION} will maneuver inside weapons range and wait — the twitch they are fishing for costs this unit its coverage, and they know the clause number as well as we do.

phases.name: THE THAW LINE
phases.lead: The contract ends on a calendar but the mission ends on the melt: forecast 11 to 18 days, {thawDay} in actuality. Whatever is on the wrong side of the lake when the ice goes stays there, and the resolution — trial, attack, or quiet — happens with the pieces already placed.

dataBlock.Thaw Forecast: 11-18 days to closure; after closure the works resupplies by air only
dataBlock.Airlift Capacity: UNCONFIRMED — basis: the spaceport manifest shows 2 civilian cargo VTOLs under charter
dataBlock.Salvage Mass: 2 OmniMech chassis at the works — any relocation is an ice-road weight problem before it is anything else

sidebarKernel.kernel: Position the spares and the food before the melt, not the week of it — the thaw does not send a batchall.

assetDetails.ref: stored Clan salvage (2 OmniMech chassis, the works)
assetDetails.detail: Chassis 1 masses 47 tons stripped, chassis 2 masses 33 tons; either one on a flatbed exceeds the ice road's 45-ton moving limit, so any relocation to the spaceport is a static-speed crossing or a 9-hour shoulder haul. Storage is legal under last contract's salvage clause and the paperwork is clean — {TARGET_FACTION} are not disputing the law, they are disputing the ownership.

Briefs verbally, never in writing, and has twice referred to the unit's salvage as 'the complication' in front of staff. Expect renewal arithmetic to weigh how the trial question was handled at least as heavily as how the world was held.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Preserve the economic corridor — spaceport, works, and road — through the reporting period. The Commonwealth measures this garrison in export tonnage and insurance posture, in that order.

clan.decisionPoints[0].context: A Star Captain of Clan Wolf has petitioned honorably for that which mercenaries hold as inventory. The trial offer is generosity. The reply will reveal whether these soldiers-for-coin understand what is being offered.

resourceGates.lackingText: No depot stocks on {WORLD}: mine and barrier materiel through the spaceport chandlers at 320,000 C-bills, delivery in 4 days — and the thaw clock does not wait for it.

title: OPERATION TALON TITHE
situation: The Khan's schedule gives this Cluster 11 days on its own before it must rejoin the advance. The Galaxy Commander has approved a Trial of Possession — a formal raid to seize a target — against the {TARGET_FACTION} depot on {WORLD}. Aerospace scouts have confirmed the target: a grounded Overlord-class DropShip loading {targetMechCount} rebuilt BattleMechs and {targetSupplyTons} tons of supplies for the enemy front. That intelligence is 6 days old and solid; the loading schedule inside it is 13 days old, so treat its timing as rough. Take those machines and they become isorla — war spoils won for the Clan, and a real blow to the enemy's next campaign. Destroy them instead and they are only wreckage with {EMPLOYER}'s name on it. That difference matters, and you will be judged on it. You won the bid to lead this. The defenders are assessed at 2 companies of BattleMechs in mixed repair, 1 armor company, and a battalion of foot soldiers with {infernoCarrierCount} missile carriers loaded with inferno rockets — fire weapons, favored by people who fight dirty. That assessment is 6 days old, so treat it as likely, not certain. {NPC:opfor-commander} commands the depot. The enemy's fighter wing at the airstrip can be airborne in 20 minutes. The ground is badlands: eroded rock mesas walling in the depot basin on the north and east. One ravine — the locals call it the choke — lets 'Mechs through single file for 2.1 kilometers under 40-meter walls. The other way in is 60 kilometers of open wheat from the west, flat and exposed, the whole distance under the depot's guns. There is no third route on the ground, and that is the whole tactical problem. Your DropShips cannot land closer than 38 kilometers without taking artillery fire on the way down. The batchall — your formal declaration of the raid — transmits the moment you commit to landing. Inner Sphere garrisons answer a batchall with silence, with lies, or with massed fire. Expect that, and let it change nothing about how you fight. Whatever you bid away before landing is your choice, and you carry the results. The recall is fixed: your DropShips lift 14 hours after landing, with the isorla or without it. The Khan's schedule does not bend for a Star Colonel's pride, quiaff?

objectives.primary: Capture the grounded Overlord's cargo: the rebuilt BattleMechs, undamaged, as war spoils.
objectives.secondary: Wreck the depot's remaining supplies so the enemy front cannot use them — without spending your bid forces on low-value targets.
objectives.bonus: Take worthy captives — MechWarriors or senior technicians, held as bondsmen — without delaying the lift.

complications.name: The Inferno Carriers
complications.text: The garrison's missile carriers fire inferno rockets and gang them onto one target at a time to swamp it with heat. It is dishonorable by Clan law — dezgra — and it works. Holding to one-on-one dueling against an enemy who burns you this way is keeping a rule he does not share.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Inferno volleys stack heat: any OmniMech hit by 2 or more carriers in one turn takes their combined heat. Declaring the carriers dezgra frees all your warriors from one-on-one dueling rules, but only against vehicles.

complications.name: Wheat Fires
complications.text: The western plain is dry-season wheat. Energy weapons and burning wrecks start crop fires that walk with the wind at 15 kilometers per hour, throwing smoke walls across the basin.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each energy-weapon hit on a plain hex has a chance to ignite it; fire and smoke spread downwind 1 hex per turn, blocking line of sight and adding heat to occupying units.

complications.name: Alert Wing at the Airstrip
complications.text: Enemy conventional fighters hold 20-minute strip alert, 270 kilometers south. They will not engage OmniMechs in the choke's walls but the open plain and the grounded DropShips are within their doctrine.
complications.mechanicalEffect: From T+0:20 after the batchall, air strikes arrive on the plain and the LZ every 4-6 turns unless the bid included aerospace cover or the strip is suppressed.

complications.name: Loading In Progress
complications.text: The Overlord is loading right now. Every hour you delay puts 2 to 3 more target 'Mechs and their crews inside a ship that can seal its doors, lift off, and end the raid with the prize aboard.
complications.mechanicalEffect: At T+8:00 the Overlord can seal and try to lift. Each hour before then moves 2 to 3 of the target 'Mechs off the depot pads and into the ship.

decisionPoints.name: The Bid
decisionPoints.context: Before you commit to landing, your Star Captains must finish bidding — competing to win the fight with the smallest force, the Clan way. The Cluster has available: 2 Trinaries of OmniMechs (about 30 'Mechs), 1 Supernova of Elementals (armored infantry), and 2 Points of fighters. The Galaxy Commander records what you bid, what you won with, and how lean the bid was. A Star Captain's reputation is built on exactly that math.

options.title: Bid Deep
advantages: One Trinary and no fighters: a bare-bones bid people will retell. Winning at this weight builds reputations and strengthens future Bloodname claims — a warrior's right to a heritage name
Fewer DropShips on the ground means a faster, cleaner lift at recall
disadvantages: Nothing answers the fighter wing except your speed and the cover of the choke's walls
If the 6-day-old count of 2 enemy 'Mech companies is too low, the bid is too weak — and asking for the reserves you gave up is itself a disgrace
options.consequence: You fight with about 15 OmniMechs against the whole depot garrison. The glory and the risk are equal, and both go on the record.

costs.resource: given up: one full Trinary, the Elemental Supernova, and both fighter Points — about 15 OmniMechs face the depot alone
costs.risk: if the 6-day-old count is too low, the bid is too weak, and calling for the reserves you gave up is a disgrace

options.title: Bid Sound
advantages: Both Trinaries with Elemental support: enough force to take the choke and the loading pads at the same time, before the Overlord seals
A safety margin against stale intelligence and Inner Sphere surprises
disadvantages: Still no fighters in the bid, so the plain and the landing zone stay open to the enemy wing
A safe bid wins no glory; it is merely enough, and the Galaxy Commander's record will say so
options.consequence: You fight with force to spare and nothing to brag about. You will likely take the prize, earn modest honor, and leave a plain line in the record.

costs.resource: given up: both fighter Points — the enemy wing flies unopposed over the plain and the landing zone
costs.risk: the bid is merely adequate; the Galaxy Commander's record will say so, and no Bloodname claim is strengthened by it

options.title: Bid the Sky
advantages: Both fighter Points included: they suppress the airstrip and take away the enemy's air power entirely
They protect the grounded DropShips, so nothing from the air can threaten your recall
disadvantages: Bidding fighters against a mere garrison depot will be called timid by every Star Captain who lost the bid
The fighters spent here are gone from the Cluster's strength for the next wave assault, where they will be missed
options.consequence: You get total force superiority — and a rumor that follows you to the next council that you bought certainty with the Khan's assets.

costs.resource: committed: both fighter Points, subtracted from the Cluster's strength for the next wave assault where they will be missed
costs.risk: every Star Captain who lost the bid will call it timid, and the rumor follows the winner to the next council

decisionPoints.name: When They Burn
decisionPoints.context: The garrison will most likely ignore your batchall and answer your assault with massed inferno fire and concentrated artillery. The first time you meet these dishonorable — dezgra — tactics, the senior warrior on the ground must decide for the whole force, on the move, with the recall clock running.

options.title: Hold Zellbrigen
advantages: Your honor stays intact no matter what the enemy does — the cleanest possible entry in the record
One-on-one discipline keeps your fire lanes clear in the choke, where a chaotic melee would be suicide
disadvantages: Fighting one target each while they gang inferno fire on you trades your warriors' lives for principle at a bad rate
It is slow: dueling your way through a whole garrison battalion may take longer than the lift window allows
options.consequence: Casualties run high, but clean. Whatever you win, you win with no asterisk, and the Remembrance will keep the story.

costs.resource: warriors and machines lost to the inferno carriers while you hold to one-on-one dueling
costs.risk: dueling through a garrison battalion may run past the T+14:00 lift, and the isorla seals inside the Overlord while you keep the forms

options.title: Declare Them Dezgra
advantages: Frees your force to concentrate fire against an enemy who is already massing theirs
The fastest way through the garrison to the loading pads before the Overlord seals
disadvantages: The call is yours and will be reviewed; a rushed one shames the whole Cluster, not just you
Once you let discipline go, it is hard to restore for the next Trial
options.consequence: The assault gets efficient and the record gets disputable. The Galaxy Commander decides later, with witnesses, whether the call was right.

costs.resource: honor: the dueling code set aside in your name, against vehicles only, before witnesses
costs.risk: a disputed call shames the Cluster and can bring a Trial of Grievance — a formal challenge — against you

options.title: Withdraw and Re-Bid
advantages: If the garrison is stronger than your bid can beat, pulling out before defeat saves the force for an honest second bid
No warrior spends his honor on a Trial that bad intelligence set up to fail
disadvantages: The recall schedule almost certainly rules out a second landing, so withdrawing likely ends the Trial with no fight at all
A Cluster that lifts off a garrison world empty-handed will hear about it from every other Cluster in the Galaxy
options.consequence: The force lifts off whole but empty. The isorla goes to feed the enemy front instead, and the bid winner owes the Galaxy Commander an explanation.

costs.resource: the isorla given up — the recall schedule almost certainly rules out a second landing
costs.risk: a Cluster that lifts off a garrison world empty-handed answers for it to every other Cluster in the Galaxy

entries.event: Batchall transmitted at descent commit; enemy depot goes to alarm regardless of reply.
the airstrip alert wing airborne; first strike window on the plain and LZ opens.
DropShips ground 38 kilometers out; advance begins toward the choke or the plain.
Earliest contact at the choke's south mouth at OmniMech cruise speed.
Overlord can complete sealing and attempt lift under battery cover.
Recall: all DropShips lift for the wave rendezvous.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: All DropShips lift at T+14:00 from grounding, carrying the isorla or leaving it. This deadline is absolute: a Star Colonel who wins the depot but misses the Galaxy's wave rendezvous has failed the mission, because the captured machines mean nothing if they are not aboard when the ships burn. Unlike the bid forces, the lift time cannot be reduced, extended, or renegotiated — plan the entire operation to finish inside the 14 hours, with recovery and loading time counted in, not added on at the end.

opforSketch.composition: Garrison-grade Inner Sphere defense scaled across the band: 2 companies of mixed-repair BattleMechs (medium-heavy, Regular, 10-25 percent understrength), 1 armor company including inferno-equipped missile carriers, dug-in conventional infantry with the depot's fixed batteries, and conventional air support on 20-minute alert. No Clan-grade equipment.
opforSketch.behavior: Static defense in depth around the pads, massed fire by doctrine, infernos against anything Clan, and no batchall reply. The commander will trade ground for time, because time is the Overlord sealing and the raiders' recall both.

forks.name: OPERATION SHRIKE LARDER
forks.trigger: The objective 'Mechs are lifted as isorla within the recall window.
forks.consequence: The Galaxy Commander assigns the Cluster the honor of first descent on the next wave world, with the captured machines issued to solahma trials — and the enemy's truce-ward front, short its resupply, grows desperate and unpredictable.

forks.name: OPERATION EMPTY TALON
forks.trigger: The Overlord lifts, seals, or burns with its cargo unclaimed.
forks.consequence: The bid winner must answer for the ratio before the Galaxy Commander. The Cluster is assigned rearguard escort for the wave — garrison work — until a Trial of redemption can be petitioned and fought at a cutdown bid.

forks.name: OPERATION GRIEVANCE CIRCLE
forks.trigger: A dezgra declaration was made and is contested in review.
forks.consequence: A rival Star Captain petitions a Trial of Grievance against the declaring warrior. The circle is fought unaugmented before the Cluster, and its result, not the depot's, is what the Remembrance keeps.

storyElementSeed: In the DropShip bay before descent, a technician kneels at an OmniMech's foot re-torquing a single bolt to specification, wipes the head clean, and chalks a tally mark beside 11 others on the armor.

phases.name: THE BID
phases.lead: The bidding closes before you commit to landing, and whatever you bid away is gone for good — there is no honorable way to take it back. The Galaxy Commander records what you bid, what you won with, and how lean the bid was. A Star Captain's reputation is built on exactly that.

dataBlock.Forces Available: 2 Trinaries of OmniMechs, 1 Supernova of Elementals, 2 Points of fighters
dataBlock.Bid Record: Sent to the Galaxy Commander when bidding closes; adding force after landing is a disgrace, not an option
dataBlock.Intelligence Age: The defense estimate is 6 days old and the loading schedule 13 days old — both likely, neither confirmed

sidebarKernel.kernel: Bid against the depot that is really there, not the one the intercepts describe. A broken bid is answered for in front of the Clusters, and 'the intelligence was stale' is no excuse the Grand Council has ever accepted.

phases.name: BATCHALL AND DESCENT
phases.lead: The batchall transmits at descent commit and the enemy goes to alarm regardless of reply — Spheroid garrisons answer with silence, with lies, or with massed fire. The DropShips ground 38 kilometers out, beyond the batteries, and the approach begins under the recall clock.

dataBlock.Grounding Distance: 38 kilometers from the depot — closer accepts battery fire on descent
dataBlock.Alert Wing: the airstrip, 270 kilometers south, airborne at T+0:20
dataBlock.Overlord Seal Threshold: T+8:00 — after which the hull can close and attempt lift under battery cover
dataBlock.Loading Rate: 2-3 objective 'Mechs move from the pads into the hull per elapsed hour

routes.name: THE CHOKE
routes.desc: 2.1 kilometers of single-file draw under 40-meter badland walls, the only covered approach from the north and east.
routes.tradeoff: The walls deny the alert wing its strafing geometry — and a column in single file fights with one machine at a time if the head of the draw is held.

routes.name: THE WHEAT ROAD
routes.desc: 60 kilometers of open dry-season wheat from the west, flat and honest, under the depot's registered artillery arcs the entire way.
routes.tradeoff: Speed and formation width, purchased under artillery and air attack across ground that burns and walks its smoke downwind at 15 kilometers per hour.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The DropShips are the recall made physical: grounded 38 kilometers out, lift at T+14:00, and no battle result alters the burn window to the wave rendezvous.

phases.name: THE TRIAL GROUND
phases.lead: The depot is taken at the pads, against a garrison that masses fire without shame and counts the Overlord's sealing as victory. What the warriors hold to in the face of inferno volleys is theirs to rule and theirs to wear afterward.
phases.protocol: A dezgra declaration is made once, by the senior warrior on the ground, transmitted in the open on the Trial frequency before witnesses, and names vehicle units only. It is not repeated, it is not delegated, and it is reviewed by the Galaxy Commander with the gun-camera record beside it.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Count the pads before you commit the Elementals. If loading has run faster than the 13-day-old schedule assumed, the isorla is already inside the ship and taking it means boarding, not raiding.

phases.name: THE LIFT
phases.lead: Recall is T+14:00 from grounding, with the isorla or without it. A Star Colonel who misses the wave rendezvous has explained nothing by winning here; the lift order is the one element of this Trial that was never bid.

dataBlock.Lift Time: T+14:00 — all DropShips burn for the wave rendezvous
dataBlock.Isorla Loading: Captured 'Mechs walk aboard under their own power or are stricken from the count; the schedule carries no winch time
dataBlock.Bondsman Boarding: Bondsmen board bound and escorted, 1 Elemental per 3, processed in transit

sidebarKernel.kernel: Powering a captured Spheroid 'Mech for the walk aboard takes a technician 20 minutes per machine if the crews left them cold — the lift schedule pays for that time, the Trial does not.

is-davion.situation.defenderNote: Depot garrison brief, other side of the hill: you have 2 understrength companies, a wing of conventional fighters, and a loading schedule the enemy has apparently read. The Overlord seals at hour 8. Everything before that is a delaying action with your name on it.

title: OPERATION HOLLOW QUIVER
situation: This mission is a trade: their supplies for a few hours of your risk. For the past 5 months, every {TARGET_FACTION} probe across the truce line has launched from one place — a forward supply depot dug into the rubble ridge at the foot of the icefield on {WORLD}, 9 kilometers from the {TARGET_FACTION} main camp. {NPC:intel-source} reports {depotAmmoTons} tons of Clan autocannon and missile ammunition, {depotArmorTons} tons of armor plate, and a 6-bay OmniMech repair line inside it. That report is 16 days old, so treat it as likely, not certain. Destroy the depot and their probes on your side of the line slow down for an estimated 2 to 3 months while they rebuild their supply line. This trade only pays once, because afterward they will rebuild the depot with a full garrison Trinary sitting on it. {EMPLOYER} is paying for that one trade with your {FORCE_SIZE}. The way in is the hard part. The depot's back is against the icefield, and the icefield is the one route the {TARGET_FACTION} treat as an obstacle instead of an open road. It is 31 kilometers of glacier, crossed by 2 marked routes that dodge the crevasses. You move at walking speed, single file, no jump jets — buried seismic sensors line the ridge, and a jump-jet landing hits the ice hard enough for them to hear it. The sensor map is 16 days old, and the routes were marked by a survey 3 years ago; the glacier drifts 40 meters a year, so the marks may be off. Downhill glacier winds ground all VTOLs — yours and theirs — from 1400 to 1700 local every day. The depot garrison is 1 solahma Star of OmniMechs, plus 2 Points of Elementals on the perimeter. Solahma are old warriors on second-line machines, posted here to die usefully; that report is also 16 days old. The front-line Trinary 9 kilometers east answers any alarm. Do not plan on duels. Solahma fight to die well, which means they all come at you at once. One order from the employer, in writing for once: prisoners the {TARGET_FACTION} take become bondsmen — captives bound into service — and a captured MechWarrior who knows our truce-line positions is a serious loss. So recovering downed pilots ranks equal with blowing the depot. Nobody gets left on the ice.

objectives.primary: Destroy the annex's munitions stock, armor stock, and refit line beyond field repair.
objectives.secondary: Recover every member of the raid force, walking or carried. Zero personnel left within the {TARGET_FACTION} occupation zone.
objectives.bonus: Haul out up to {haulTons} tons of Clan armor plate or weapons salvage on the exit sleds — only if doing so does not slow the escape.

complications.name: The Glacier Clock
complications.text: Both marked routes are walking-speed, single-file, and 3 years out of date against a glacier that drifts 40 meters a year. An unmarked crevasse drops a 'Mech to the hip or worse, and pulling it out takes hours you do not have once the alarm goes.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Movement on the icefield is capped at walking speed in column; any deviation from the flagged route triggers a crevasse check per hex. Jump jet use anywhere on the ice or moraine triggers the seismic net and starts the reaction timeline immediately.

complications.name: Katabatic Window
complications.text: Glacier outflow winds ground all rotary and VTOL aircraft from 1400 to 1700 local daily. This is the only guaranteed period in which the {TARGET_FACTION} cantonment cannot put eyes or Elemental-carrier lift over the icefield.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Between 1400 and 1700 local, neither side may operate VTOL or aerospace assets below 3,000 meters. Outside that window, {TARGET_FACTION} aerial reconnaissance sweeps the ice every 90 minutes.

complications.name: Solahma Garrison
complications.text: The annex Star is old warriors on second-line machines, posted here to die usefully. They will not duel, they will not withdraw, and they will mass fire on the first target that breaches the wire.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Garrison units ignore zellbrigen, never check morale, and fight to destruction. Treat all garrison fire as concentrated by doctrine.

complications.name: Cook-Off Radius
complications.text: {depotAmmoTons} tons of Clan ammunition goes off all at once when it burns. The demolition plan has to allow for a blast that reaches the repair line, the perimeter fence, and any raider still inside it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Once charges are set, detonation produces a 4-hex destruction radius and an 8-hex damage radius; any unit inside at T-0 takes the corresponding damage. Timed fuses are fixed at 10 minutes once armed.

decisionPoints.name: How It Burns
decisionPoints.context: The annex can be destroyed three ways, and the choice sets the egress clock. The demolition officer wants a decision before the force leaves the ice, not at the wire.

options.title: Charges and a Sweep
advantages: Total destruction, confirmed by eyes-on: munitions, armor stock, and refit line in one engineered demolition
The 10-minute fuse window doubles as the egress head start
disadvantages: Requires holding the annex interior for an estimated 25-35 minutes against the solahma garrison
Every minute inside the wire is a minute the cantonment Trinary closes the 9 kilometers
options.consequence: Maximum certainty, maximum exposure. The raid succeeds or fails inside the wire, and the fight there is to the garrison's last machine.

costs.resource: engineered demolition sets for the munitions stock, armor stock, and refit line, hand-placed on the fixed 10-minute fuses
costs.risk: 25-35 minutes inside the wire against a garrison that fights to destruction, with the cantonment Trinary 9 kilometers out

options.title: Stand-Off Bombardment
advantages: LRM and PPC fire from the moraine crest never enters the wire at all
Engagement can begin and end inside the katabatic window with no aerial response possible
disadvantages: No proof of the kill: hardened bays shrug off indirect fire, and the repair line may survive behind the ridge berm
You spend a lot of ammunition for a likely partial result — and the trade stops being worth it
options.consequence: Low risk, but you cannot confirm the result. Orbital assessment comes back in 4 days, and a PARTIAL grade is the likeliest outcome.

costs.resource: the raid force's full LRM and PPC ammunition allocation, fired from the moraine crest for a probable partial
costs.risk: no confirmation until orbital assessment in 4 days — hardened bays shrug indirect fire and the refit line may survive

options.title: Take the Refit Line First
advantages: Holding the 6-bay repair line intact for 40 minutes lets the techs strip {haulTons} tons of Clan parts before the charges go in
That salvage pays for the raid twice over, and the employer's quartermasters get Clan spares
disadvantages: Those 40 extra minutes inside the fence run past the enemy Trinary's arrival, so a running fight on the way out is certain, not just possible
Loaded exit sleds cut your speed on the ice routes by a third
options.consequence: The raid becomes a full assault with a salvage stage. Everything still burns, but you pay for the bonus in armor and maybe pilots.

costs.resource: 40 additional minutes inside the wire and a third off ice-route speed on loaded egress sleds
costs.risk: fighting withdrawal guaranteed past the cantonment Trinary's arrival window — a captured pilot is a bondsman, not a line item

entries.event: Alarm — seismic trip, wire contact, or first shot, whichever comes first. Annex garrison stands to in place.
Cantonment QRF — 1 OmniMech Star — rolls from the east at flank speed.
QRF Star reaches the annex perimeter via the moraine road.
Full cantonment Trinary committed; Elemental carriers lift if outside the katabatic window.
{TARGET_FACTION} aerospace overflies the icefield routes if outside the katabatic window; egress columns on the ice are naked to it.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The raid force must be off the icefield and scattered into the ridge canyons by T+4:00 from the alarm, before the next aerial sweep can pin down the escape route. After T+4:00, every remaining choice costs you pilots to gain distance.

opforSketch.composition: At the annex: 1 solahma Star of second-line OmniMechs plus 2 Points of Elementals on fixed defenses, scaled to the band by equipment age rather than numbers. Response echelon: 1 front-line OmniMech Star at T+0:22, building to a full Trinary with Elemental support by T+0:40, aerospace outside the katabatic window.
opforSketch.behavior: The garrison masses fire and dies in place without honor rules. The response echelon fights front-line Clan doctrine — fast, direct, contemptuous of a raider's rearguard — and will pursue onto the ice exactly as far as their own crevasse maps allow, which is farther than yours.

forks.name: OPERATION SECOND INVOICE
forks.trigger: Annex destroyed with confirmation and zero personnel lost to capture.
forks.consequence: The probe tempo collapses as projected, and the employer commits to the follow-on: a matched raid against the replacement depot while its garrison is still pouring concrete — smaller target, angrier {TARGET_FACTION}.

forks.name: OPERATION COLD RECEIPT
forks.trigger: Any raid personnel captured, or the annex left functionally intact.
forks.consequence: Captured pilots enter bondsman processing at the cantonment, with transfer off-world estimated in 10-14 days. The recovery operation goes onto the board immediately, against a target that now expects exactly that.

forks.name: OPERATION QUIVER AUDIT
forks.trigger: Stand-off bombardment chosen or demolition unconfirmed.
forks.consequence: Orbital assessment in 4 days grades the damage. If the refit line survived, the employer offers the books-balancing option: go back in across the same ice, against a garrison that has re-strung the sensor net.

storyElementSeed: On the night ice, the column halts while a tech on foot probes the snow ahead of the lead 'Mech with a 3-meter pole, planting a green flag every 20 paces, breath freezing on the inside of the face mask.

phases.name: INGRESS — THE ICE
phases.lead: 31 kilometers of glacier at walking speed, single file, following route markers a survey planted 3 years ago. The glacier has drifted 40 meters a year since, so the markers could be off by up to 120 meters. Plan on checking every one before you trust it.

routes.name: ROUTE CAIRN
routes.desc: The northern flagged line: 31 kilometers, 14 hours at column walking speed, ending in the moraine canyons 6 kilometers from the annex wire.
routes.tradeoff: Shorter final approach; crosses 2 known crevasse fields where the 3-year drift is worst.

routes.name: ROUTE FERRIER
routes.desc: The southern flagged line: 36 kilometers, 16 hours, tracking the icefield's stable spine to a canyon mouth 9 kilometers from the wire.
routes.tradeoff: Better ice, longer ground exposure — 3 additional kilometers inside the seismic net's outer ring.

dataBlock.Crevasse Procedure: The lead element probes and re-marks the route; a 'Mech through the crust takes hours you do not have once the alarm goes

phases.name: GROUND — THE ANNEX
phases.lead: The wire is held by old warriors posted here to die usefully, and they will all fight at once. However it burns, the demolition decision was made back on the ice — the ground phase just pays for it.

dataBlock.Cantonment Response: QRF Star rolls at T+0:06 from alarm, at the wire by T+0:22; full Trinary committed by T+0:40

phases.name: EXTRACTION — OFF THE ICE
phases.lead: Everything off the icefield and dispersed into the moraine canyons by T+4:00 from alarm, before the next aerial sweep can fix the egress route. The recovery priority is written into the objectives, so the rearguard plan is a casualty plan first and a fighting plan second.
phases.protocol: Pilot-down drill: the column halts for no single machine — the designated winch pair (2 'Mechs, tow gear staged) breaks off, the rest keep walking. A pilot who cannot ride rides a sled; a sled that slows the column below schedule drops salvage, not people. Egress confirmation by short-burst only, 2 clicks at each route flag, no voice traffic on the ice.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Cold injuries on the egress will outnumber gunshot wounds 3 to 1 — every casualty goes onto a sled warmed, splinted, and moving within 40 minutes, because the ice does {TARGET_FACTION}'s work for free.

merc.objectives.secondary: Everybody comes home. Read the contract's capture clause before you plan the rearguard: bondsman status is not a recoverable line item, and the employer's repatriation rider lapses at the truce line.

is-kurita.objectives.secondary: No warrior of the Dragon is left to become another Clan's property. Recovery of the fallen is not a sentiment; it is the difference between a raid and a disgrace.

resourceGates.lackingText: No owned DropShip tonnage at the recovery point: the employer's charter lifts personnel only, and {haulTons} tons of Clan salvage has nowhere to go.
The unit cannot replace the LRM and PPC stocks this fire plan consumes; below a 250,000 C-bill reserve the bombardment is off the board.

title: OPERATION VESPER AUDIT
situation: A count you verify is worth something; a count you only repeat is worth nothing. ComStar — the Blessed Order — runs the civil side of {WORLD} for its {TARGET_FACTION} occupiers under a formal deal called the Terms: the census, food distribution, and the HPG relay station. In return, the {TARGET_FACTION} report their garrison strength to our administrators, and the Precentor Martial's staff no longer believes those numbers. They claim 1 Cluster, spread out. But the tithe records, the smelter district's power bills, and the grain orders all point to more than that — a force gathering to move. Where the paperwork disagrees, someone has to go and count in person. {EMPLOYER} needs a physical count of 3 sites: the {TARGET_FACTION} camp at the mine head, the DropShip landing yard on the slag plain, and the rail switching yard. The site data is 12 days old and reliable, but the camp figure comes from a single worker's tally taken 26 days ago — treat that one as a rough guess. What you must bring back: OmniMechs counted by weight class, DropShips by hull class, and Elemental strength to the nearest Point, each backed by a photo or a sensor log. Your {FORCE_SIZE} travels under ComStar civil cover. The transit passes are real, issued by {NPC:employer-contact}, who has no idea what they are for and must never find out — for the Order's safety and his own. The terrain both hides you and traps you. The smelter district's waste terraces step down the valley in 14 shelves, each 40 meters high, linked by switchback ramps one vehicle wide. The shelves throw hard radar shadow over everything below the working rim, and the ore conveyors jam magnetic sensors within 2 kilometers of any running line. But in the dry season the terrace dust holds tracks for 6 days, and a hot machine glows on a shelf wall from 8 kilometers off. You can hide the machines in the shadows; you cannot hide their footprints. The {TARGET_FACTION} run sibko patrols — cadet trainees, still children by their reckoning — through the district on no fixed schedule, and you cannot tell a training sweep from a real one until it turns toward you. One rule is absolute: if the {TARGET_FACTION} capture ComStar people or passes while they are armed, the Terms collapse on {WORLD} and the Order loses its role on 11 worlds with them. The count must be true and the counters must stay deniable. So the whole order is three words: be invisible, be exact, be gone.

objectives.primary: Deliver backed-up counts — OmniMechs by weight class, DropShips by hull, Elementals by Point — for all 3 sites to the HPG station before the scheduled transmission window.
objectives.secondary: Leave no trace: no fighting, no captured military gear, and no witness who can tie armed people to ComStar passes.
objectives.bonus: Grab a power or fuel record from inside the camp that shows when the {TARGET_FACTION} will be ready to launch.

complications.name: Dust Ledger
complications.text: The terrace dust records every track for 6 days in dry season. The benches hide a machine from radar and eyes; they cannot hide where it has walked. A sibko patrol that crosses your trace will follow it as a lesson in tracking.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Every hex traversed by vehicle or 'Mech leaves a trace marker persisting the whole mission; any {TARGET_FACTION} patrol crossing a trace follows it toward its source. Foot movement leaves no marker on ramp and bench hexes.

complications.name: Conveyor Interference
complications.text: Active ore conveyors blind magnetic-anomaly detection within 2 kilometers — both sides' detection. The conveyors run on the smelter schedule, not yours, and a line that halts mid-shift is itself an anomaly the pit office will report.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Within 2 kilometers of an active conveyor, all magnetic and seismic sensors are inoperative for all units. If a conveyor is stopped by any player action, the pit office alerts the cantonment within 30 minutes.

complications.name: Sibko Sweeps
complications.text: Training patrols of sibko cadets under a single instructor cross the district on no fixed schedule. They are unblooded, eager, and graded on initiative. An instructor who confirms contact will not wait for the cantonment.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Roll each mission day for 1-2 patrol crossings (3-5 light OmniMechs or 2 Elemental Points each). Patrols that gain a contact attack immediately and transmit position; the reaction timeline starts on their transmission.

complications.name: The Passes
complications.text: The transit passes are genuine and traceable to {NPC:employer-contact}. Used at a checkpoint, they work; recovered from a corpse or a captured vehicle, they unravel the Order's standing on {WORLD} and 10 worlds beside it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any scenario result that leaves personnel, vehicles, or documents in {TARGET_FACTION} custody forces the COMPROMISED gate regardless of data delivered.

decisionPoints.name: The Manner of Counting
decisionPoints.context: Three sites, one transmission window, and three doctrines of audit on the table. The cell leader must commit the method before insertion; the sites are too far apart to improvise twice.

options.title: Eyes and Glass
advantages: Pure observation from the bench shadows: no emissions, no entry, nothing to recover if it fails
Foot teams on the terraces leave no dust trace
disadvantages: Counts from 800-meter standoff cannot resolve DropShip hull classes through slag haze with confidence above MEDIUM
Three sites by foot infiltration consumes 5 of the 6 days before the transmission window
options.consequence: Deliverables arrive deniable but graded MEDIUM confidence — sufficient for the audit, insufficient to overrule {TARGET_FACTION}'s own declaration if challenged.

costs.risk: three sites by foot consume 5 of the 6 days before the window — one missed march and the data misses the transmission entirely

options.title: Seed the Benches
advantages: Remote sensor packages on benches 4, 9, and 12 count everything that moves for the rest of the occupation, not just this week
Emplacement takes 2 nights; the cell is gone before the data is even interesting
disadvantages: The packages are manufactured items with no administrative cover story if found
Conveyor interference gaps the coverage; the count will have holes a careful analyst must flag
options.consequence: A standing intelligence asset is created and a standing piece of evidence with it. The audit succeeds unless and until a sibko exercise digs in the wrong bench.

costs.resource: 3 remote sensor packages — manufactured items with no administrative cover story if found
costs.risk: each package is standing evidence against the Order for the remainder of the occupation

options.title: Borrow the Census
advantages: The Order's own civil administration database, accessed from inside the compound, already holds fuel, food, and labor allocations that imply exact garrison strength
No one approaches a {TARGET_FACTION} site at all; HIGH confidence by triangulation
disadvantages: Using the Order's own civil records for spying is exactly what the Terms forbid — if it comes out, it splits the compound from within, not just angers the enemy outside
{NPC:employer-contact} or his staff may spot the database queries within days
options.consequence: The count is exact, but the wrong done is the Order's own. The data goes out, and so does the question of what this cost the Order's neutrality — left for better heads to answer, or worse ones.

costs.resource: the Order's neutrality: consecrated administrative records turned to military intelligence
costs.risk: the query trail may surface under {NPC:employer-contact}'s staff within days — discovery means schism inside the compound

entries.event: Contact transmitted — by patrol, pit office, or checkpoint. Cantonment duty Star stands to.
First OmniMech Point reaches the nearest terrace ramp; ramps are the only vehicle descent, and they know it.
Elemental Points begin bench-by-bench descent on foot lines — the route a machine cannot watch.
District cordon complete; all switchback ramps held.
Scheduled HPG transmission window — duration 11 minutes.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The audit data can only leave the world during the scheduled HPG transmission window, which opens at T+54:00 from insertion and lasts just 11 minutes. There is no second chance this mission: the next available window is 9 days later, after the Precentor Martial's compilation date has already passed. Counts that miss the window cannot be sent in time to matter, so the mission fails even if every site was counted perfectly. Plan every march backward from that 11-minute window — it is the one deadline nothing else can flex around.

opforSketch.composition: Garrison presence scaled to the band: sibko training patrols of 3-5 light OmniMechs or 2 Elemental Points as roving contacts; a duty Star of mixed OmniMechs as the cantonment reaction echelon; Elemental Points for terrain the machines cannot reach. No artillery, no aerospace below orbital tasking — {TARGET_FACTION} do not believe anything on {WORLD} warrants it.
opforSketch.behavior: Contemptuous and procedural until contact is confirmed, then fast and total. Sibko patrols overpursue by doctrine and by youth. The cantonment treats any armed contact as a possible Inner Sphere raid and cordons the terraces rather than chasing through them.

forks.name: OPERATION COMPLINE
forks.trigger: All 3 counts delivered corroborated, no evidence left, window met.
forks.consequence: The audit changes the Precentor Martial's arithmetic for the coming trial of arms. The cell is retasked to courier the consolidated annex through {TARGET_FACTION}-administered space to a collection point 2 jumps out — quiet work carrying loud cargo.

forks.name: OPERATION LENTEN HOUSE
forks.trigger: The window is missed or the counts arrive uncorroborated.
forks.consequence: The Order must hold the question open 9 more days on a world that may be staging for lift. The cell winters in place under administrative cover with ROM counter-audit teams inbound to find out what went wrong — starting with everyone the passes touched.

forks.name: OPERATION BROKEN SEAL
forks.trigger: Personnel, equipment, or passes left in {TARGET_FACTION} custody.
forks.consequence: The Terms are in question on 11 worlds. The cell must be extracted off {WORLD} by unregistered lift before {TARGET_FACTION} finish connecting the passes to the compound — and before the Order decides denial is cheaper than rescue.

storyElementSeed: In the bench shadow at dawn, an observer cleans slag dust from a camera lens with a prayer-cloth, logs the seventh DropShip silhouette of the shift, and underlines the count twice before believing it.

phases.name: ENTRY IN COVER
phases.lead: The passes are real and the cover is civilian, and losing either is paid for by 11 worlds. Enter the way the Order travels everywhere: on schedule, on paper, and completely ordinary.
phases.protocol: Carry the transit passes on your body; never stash them, never copy them. At checkpoints: present the pass, answer in the clerk's own routine language, and volunteer nothing. If any team member is held longer than 40 minutes, the rest walk the abort route and the count is rescheduled. Never leave a pass in a vehicle, a shelter, or a grave.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Every checkpoint logs your passes against the compound's records within 24 hours. The cover is not that you are invisible — it is that you are boring, and a boring record has to stay consistent to hold.

phases.name: THE COUNT
phases.lead: Three sites, and each count needs backup or it is just rumor. A count you verify is worth something; anything you only estimate, mark clearly as an estimate and say what it is based on.

dataBlock.Site 1 — Camp: OmniMech count by weight class; compare against the declared 45 (the worker's tally is 26 days old — treat as a rough guess)
dataBlock.Site 2 — Slag Plain Annex: DropShip count by hull class; slag haze degrades standoff identification beyond 800 meters
dataBlock.Site 3 — Rail Yard: Elemental strength to the nearest Point; rail tonnage flow as corroboration
dataBlock.Terrace Geometry: 14 benches at 40 meters, switchback ramps one vehicle wide; dust holds tracks 6 days; thermal blooms visible at 8 kilometers

sidebarKernel.kernel: The ledgers say 60 to 90 machines where 45 are declared — the audit's purpose is not to find the truth, it is to make the truth provable to a Precentor Martial who will stake worlds on it.

phases.name: THE WINDOW
phases.lead: The transmission window opens at T+54:00 and lasts 11 minutes, and the next one is not for another 9 days. Data that misses this window cannot reach the Precentor Martial in time to be acted on, so a missed window means the whole audit fails regardless of how good the counts are.
phases.protocol: Deliverables travel to the HPG compound as registry corrections in the civil format, hand-carried, checksummed against the courier's memorized digest. Transmission rides the scheduled traffic — no priority flag, no added length, nothing a {TARGET_FACTION} traffic analyst would tithe a second look. If the window is missed, the material is sealed into the registry archive and the cell disperses to administrative postings until the next compilation date.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Plan every march backward from the last minute of the 11-minute window. That deadline cannot move, so every other deadline has to bend around it.

assetDetails.detail: Issued the transit passes as routine administrative instruments and must never learn their use; their staff reconciles pass logs monthly, so every checkpoint presentation must match a plausible registry errand on the compound's own books.

Counted machines through a mess-hall window over 6 shifts, 26 days ago, and has not been re-contacted since — the Order's rules forbid re-approach during an active audit. The count is the audit's weakest figure and its only inside one.

merc.objectives.secondary: Deniability is the deliverable. The employer's passes work until they are found on you, at which point the contract's existence becomes a theological question and your bond becomes a rounding error.

is-davion.situation.tasking: MIIO would phrase it shorter: the Jaguars are lying about their strength on {WORLD}, the ledgers prove it indirectly, and someone has to stand on a terrace and count the actual iron.

dropShipCount.unit: DropShips on the slag plain annex

resourceGates.lackingText: No quartermaster issue available off-compound: equivalent sensor packages procured through gray-market channels at 135,000 C-bills, with a purchase trail the audit itself would flag.

title: OPERATION SILENT TALLY
situation: The contract is 9 pages; the mission is one sentence: find out whether the {TARGET_FACTION} are massing on {WORLD} to push across the truce line. {EMPLOYER} is a purchasing office that has never purchased anything, working through {NPC:employer-contact}, a broker who bills from 3 different addresses. They want DropShip counts at the spaceport, supply-tonnage estimates at the rail depot, and photos of both. What they are really buying is a number to set against the number the diplomats have been given, because the two do not match. The diplomats' figure is 40 days old, and by the broker's own admission, worthless. Read clause 11 before you pack. This contract does not officially exist; the employer will deny it; and capture voids your recovery clause completely. A merc caught under arms in the occupation zone is a truce violation with your face on it, and for once both governments will quickly agree you were freelancing. The pay runs the other way from the risk: verified hull-class counts pay triple your base rate, and a clean exit with no contact pays a bonus on top. They are not paying you to fight. They are paying you to be a rumor. The ground is glacial ridge country — parallel gravel ridges 15 to 30 meters high, spaced 600 to 1,100 meters apart, with marsh and stunted birch between them, running northwest to southeast. Move along the ridges and they hide you all the way to the overlook — but the ridge lines squeeze together at 4 river fords where the patrol routes cross, and the {TARGET_FACTION} know those chokepoints. Move across the ridges instead and you show your silhouette at every crest, every 800 meters. The garrison is 1 second-line {TARGET_FACTION} Cluster, stiffened with solahma — old warriors — and, per the broker's local contacts, sibko trainees on their first posting. That intelligence is 21 days old, so treat it as likely, not certain. Second-line does not mean slow; it means they have something to prove and a Khan who is not watching closely. The local civilians are friendly, talkative, and infiltrated. Assume one informer per village and treat every barn you shelter in as a risk. Pickup is a chartered coastal boat at the coastal landing: one pass, 40 minutes at the dock, 72 hours after you insert. The captain has been paid to think he is carrying fish, and he will wait exactly as long as a man carrying fish would wait.

objectives.primary: Deliver verified DropShip counts by hull class at the spaceport and tonnage-flow estimates at the rail depot, with imagery, to the extraction point by T+72:00.
objectives.secondary: Zero contact: no engagement with {TARGET_FACTION} forces, no sensor lock held longer than 10 seconds, no physical evidence of the unit's presence in the zone.
objectives.bonus: Work out whether the rail depot's stockpile looks like preparation to attack (bridging units, fuel pushed forward of the railhead) or just a routine garrison swap — the one question the employer actually cares about.

complications.name: Esker Grain
complications.text: The ridges shelter movement along their axis and betray it across. The route plan is a geometry problem with 4 mandatory fords where {TARGET_FACTION} patrol tracks cross the ridge lines, and the marsh between ridges swallows wheeled vehicles whole.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Movement along ridge-shadow hexes is concealed from ground sensors; any cross-grain movement skylines the unit for 1 turn per ridge crossed, visible to 4 kilometers. Wheeled vehicles bog in marsh hexes on anything but frozen ground.

complications.name: First-Posting Patrols
complications.text: Sibko trainees ride the patrol circuits under solahma instructors. The trainees overpursue; the instructors let them, because that is the lesson. A contact that should cost you 10 minutes can become a 30-kilometer chase with a teaching staff grading it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: {TARGET_FACTION} patrol units never break off pursuit voluntarily; each patrol contact rolls to escalate, adding 1 additional patrol to the search pattern for the rest of the mission.

complications.name: One Informer Per Settlement
complications.text: The local population hates the occupation and feeds it anyway — labor scrip buys food, and a tip buys scrip. Shelter, directions, or a borrowed truck are all available and all priced in risk.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each interaction with a settlement rolls for an informer report reaching the garrison in 6-12 hours, adding patrol density along the unit's last reported axis.

decisionPoints.name: The Way In
