decisionPoints.context: Three insertion plans survived the planning weekend. The broker priced all three and declined, in writing, to recommend any. The choice fixes the extraction geometry too — the hauler waits at the coastal landing regardless.

options.title: Manifest Cover
advantages: Riding a ComStar-chartered grain freighter into the spaceport civil field puts the team 11 kilometers from the first objective with paperwork that survives a checkpoint glance
No burn signature, no coastal sensor line, nothing to explain
disadvantages: No weapons heavier than sidearms clear the cargo inspection — the recon is done naked
If the cover breaks, it breaks ComStar's charter too, and clause 11 starts applying to people who never signed it
options.consequence: The team operates inside the occupation's own logistics with nothing but glass, wits, and the silence premium riding on every checkpoint.

costs.resource: all weapons heavier than sidearms left behind — the recon is done naked
costs.risk: a broken cover breaks ComStar's charter with it, and clause 11 starts applying to people who never signed

options.title: Polar Cache Walk
advantages: Insertion by long-dwell skiff onto the tundra cap, then 140 kilometers south on muscle and stored fuel from a pre-occupation survey cache the broker swears is intact
Approach axis no patrol circuit covers; full equipment comes along
disadvantages: 5 days of transit eats the timeline to the bone — the T+72:00 clock starts at insertion, not at the cache
If the cache is stripped, the plan dies 140 kilometers from anywhere, quietly
options.consequence: Maximum equipment and maximum margin against contact, purchased with the entire schedule reserve. Everything after the cache must run on rails.

costs.resource: the pre-occupation survey cache's stored fuel — the entire schedule reserve rides on a 3-year-old inventory the broker swears by
costs.risk: if the cache is stripped, the plan dies 140 kilometers from anywhere, quietly

options.title: Pirate-Point Sprint
advantages: In fast, out fast: skiff down from a calculated point, 30 hours on the ground, the hauler pickup becomes a backup instead of a lifeline
Shortest exposure window of the three by a factor of 2
disadvantages: The descent plume is a sensor event; the garrison may not identify it but will log it and seed the patrol schedule with suspicion
Pirate-point arithmetic over an occupied world: a transit mishap is not a delay, it is a headline
options.consequence: Speed buys safety from the ground threat and spends it on the descent. The mission runs against an alerted patrol pattern from hour zero.

costs.resource: the descent plume — a sensor event the garrison logs and seeds the patrol schedule with
costs.risk: pirate-point arithmetic over an occupied world: a transit mishap is not a delay, it is a headline

entries.event: Contact event — patrol sighting, informer report actioned, or sensor lock held past 10 seconds.
Nearest patrol vectors in; sibko elements accelerate ahead of their instructor's plan.
Garrison duty Star augments the search; ford crossings picketed.
Search pattern matures: ridge-line overwatch points manned, settlement sweeps begin.
Hauler at the coastal landing. Dwell 40 minutes. One pass.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The boat leaves the coastal landing at T+72:40 with or without you, and there is no second charter — the broker's note makes that very clear. Miss it and the unit has to walk out of an occupied zone on foot, with the data going stale in its pockets.

opforSketch.composition: Second-line {TARGET_FACTION} garrison force scaled to the band: patrol elements of 2-3 OmniMechs or hover vehicles with sibko riders, a duty Star of mixed second-line OmniMechs, Elemental Points at the spaceport and depot proper. No aerospace patrol below high cover; {TARGET_FACTION} do not advertise what the spaceport holds either.
opforSketch.behavior: Patrols hunt enthusiastically and report late, trying to bag the contact themselves. The duty Star fights with {TARGET_FACTION} precision and no honor pageantry against an unannounced intruder — a spy is dezgra by definition and gets the efficient version.

forks.name: OPERATION TRIPLE RATE
forks.trigger: Counts and imagery delivered, zero contact, hauler made.
forks.consequence: The numbers do not match the diplomatic figure, exactly as feared. The employer exercises the option clause: a return engagement to watch the same ground across the thaw, at triple rate, because now both sides of the line know someone counted.

forks.name: OPERATION QUIET INVOICE
forks.trigger: Personnel captured or evidence of the unit left in the zone.
forks.consequence: Clause 11 executes: disavowal in 48 hours, recovery rider void. The captured are paraded as truce-breakers on {TARGET_FACTION} broadcasts. Whatever rescue happens is private, unpaid, and planned by whoever is left.

forks.name: OPERATION STALE BREAD
forks.trigger: Data delivered late or below verification standard.
forks.consequence: Base rate only, silence premium void, and the broker's next call offers the gap-filling job: a closer look at the rail depot specifically, on a compressed clock, against the patrol density the first visit created.

storyElementSeed: In a birch stand between ridges, two crew members count rail cars through a spotting scope in whispered turns, marking tallies on the inside of a forearm because paper rattles in the wind.

phases.name: INSERTION
phases.lead: Three ways in, all priced, none recommended — in writing. Whatever the choice, the T+72:00 clock starts at insertion, and every hour of it spent traveling is an hour not spent counting.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Pick the insertion for the extraction it leaves behind: the hauler waits at the coastal landing for everybody, and 2 of the 3 ways in put the team on the wrong side of 4 patrolled fords when it is time to walk out.

phases.name: THE OVERLOOK
phases.lead: The esker country moves you or betrays you, nothing in between. Work the grain northwest to the overlook, count, photograph, and spend sensor time like it bills by the second — because per the contract, it does.

routes.name: RIDGE SHADOW
routes.desc: Along-grain movement in the esker shadows, 600 to 1,100 meters of marsh and birch between ridges, funneling through 4 fords where {TARGET_FACTION} patrol circuits cross.
routes.tradeoff: Concealed the whole way; the fords are the whole risk, and {TARGET_FACTION} know their own funnels.

routes.name: CROSS GRAIN
routes.desc: Direct lines toward the spaceport or the rail depot, skylining every 800 meters at each ridge crest.
routes.tradeoff: Hours saved against a silhouette visible to 4 kilometers — a target drone on a rail, per the planning notes.

dataBlock.Deliverable 1: the spaceport DropShip count by hull class, with imagery
dataBlock.Deliverable 2: the rail depot tonnage flow estimate against the {viborgTonnageDaily} tons-per-day band, with imagery
dataBlock.Sensor Discipline: No active emission; no sensor lock held longer than 10 seconds
dataBlock.Settlement Pricing: Assume 1 informer per settlement; any contact reaches the garrison in 6-12 hours

sidebarKernel.kernel: The bonus question is the real contract: bridging units and fuel forward of the railhead mean they are preparing to attack; ordinary garrison stores mean a routine swap. Count the hulls, but photograph what is stacked on the loading docks.

phases.name: THE HAULER
phases.lead: One pass, 40 minutes of dwell, T+72:00 at the coastal landing. The captain has been paid for fish and will wait exactly like a man paid for fish.
phases.protocol: Recognition: the hauler shows deck working lights and a single amber masthead repeat — board only if the amber is lit; a white masthead means stand off, the captain has company. Team signal is 2 long flashes from the south breakwater at H-10 minutes. No radio between team and hauler at any point; the charter's only codeword, GULLCATCH, is for cancellation, passes through the broker, and means swim or winter over.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The dwell is 40 minutes including the tide turn — gear that cannot be carried down the breakwater at a jog in 2 trips should have been buried with the rest of the evidence.

assetDetails.detail: Bills from 3 addresses, declined in writing to recommend an insertion plan, and holds the only channel for the GULLCATCH cancellation — which means the broker can end the mission and the unit cannot. Price that asymmetry into every report sent back.

Paid for fish, asks only fish questions, and owns the only hull on the coast that makes the pickup deniable. If the team boards hot, his ignorance stops being plausible and the silence premium stops being payable — the recovery rider does not cover witnesses who change their minds at sea.

is-steiner.objectives.bonus: The Commonwealth's analysts require the staging-versus-rotation determination above all: bridging assets and forward fuel are the signature of intent, and intent is what the Archon's council is actually purchasing.

comstar.objectives.secondary: Let nothing be written in the world that was not first written in the plan. An unobserved auditor is the only honest one.

viborgTonnageDaily.unit: tons per day through the rail depot

patrolCircuits.unit: active Wolf patrol circuits in the esker country

resourceGates.lackingText: No organic small craft: the broker's long-dwell skiff charter adds 45,000 C-bills and fixes the insertion date to the charter's schedule, not yours.
No owned JumpShip: the broker's pirate-point charter quotes 290,000 C-bills, half in advance, captain unnamed — and the silence premium now has a witness.

title: OPERATION SACRED FREIGHT
situation: The ilKhan is dead over {WORLD}, and the invasion has halted while the Clans choose his successor. The Galaxy lifts for the homeward jump in 60 hours. But a debt remains on the ground. During the pullback to orbit, the BattleMech of {NPC:fallen-warrior} — a Bloodnamed, twice-honored warrior carrying a name held since the Clan's founding — went down in the marshes with its pilot dead in the cockpit. The recovery team was ambushed at the wreck by a battalion of {TARGET_FACTION} regulars who never accepted their government's surrender and feel bound by nothing signed in a city they have abandoned. They have winched the 'Mech onto a rail flatcar at the rail yard, with the body still aboard. We know where it is going: the hardened research complex under the mountain, where Inner Sphere technicians will cut open both the machine and the warrior to learn what they can. That intelligence is 3 days old and solid, taken from intercepted rail traffic; the train leaves sometime within a 30-hour window. Understand what is on that flatcar. The machine is only salvage — we have won and lost machines since the Exodus, and it means little. The giftake means everything. The giftake is the dead warrior's genetic legacy, and it belongs to the Clan, to the sacred bloodline, to future Trials of Bloodright not yet fought. Leaving it to be dissected in an Inner Sphere lab is not a defeat — it is a desecration, and every warrior in the Galaxy knows it is out there. The Loremaster has set the bid at 1 Star of OmniMechs and 1 Point of Elementals — armored infantry. This is a recovery, not a conquest, and the election recall does not slow down for grief. The ground favors the dead. The marshes are frozen-crust peat: 'Mechs of 60 tons and under cross at walking speed, but heavier machines break through into 1.5 meters of black water and stay stuck until winched out. The rail causeway is the only heavy-rated line through the marsh — single track, 7 meters above the bog on driven pilings, with the armored train on it now. The {TARGET_FACTION} fight in the shadow of their own martyr: the pilot who rammed the ilKhan's flagship and killed a Khan with a fighter's hull. They believe dying well is winning. They are not entirely wrong, and that is what makes them dangerous, quiaff?

objectives.primary: Recover the giftake and the remains of {NPC:fallen-warrior} before the train reaches the complex.
objectives.secondary: Recover the 'Mech's codex core — its warrior's record — intact. Keep the chassis from the enemy: recover it if you can, destroy it if you cannot.
objectives.bonus: Finish the recovery without firing on the train's civilian rail crew — conscripted track workers, not soldiers, per the intercepts.

complications.name: Crust Weight Limit
complications.text: The fen crust carries 60 tons at a walk and nothing more. The bid Star's composition was chosen before this fact was fully mapped; any heavy OmniMech in the Star is confined to the causeway approaches and the yard itself.
complications.mechanicalEffect: 'Mechs over 60 tons entering fen hexes break through: immobilized until winched (3 turns, one adjacent unit assisting). 'Mechs at 60 tons or under move at walking speed only in fen hexes; running triggers a breakthrough check.

complications.name: The Armored Train
complications.text: Two gun wagons bracket the flatcar — turreted autocannon and a mast-mounted searchlight battery — with an armored locomotive at each end. On the causeway it cannot maneuver, but it cannot be flanked from the bog by anything heavy enough to stop it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The train moves on the causeway at fixed speed each turn while either locomotive lives. Gun wagons fire as fixed turrets. Derailment or locomotive kills stop the train but risk toppling the flatcar — roll for cargo damage to the objective.

complications.name: Martyr Doctrine
complications.text: The remnant battalion has stopped counting odds. Expect satchel-charge infantry rushes against OmniMech legs, inferno fire from the trestle shadows, and zero response to any demonstration of force meant to encourage surrender.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Remnant units never check morale and never withdraw. Infantry in trestle and bog hexes deploy hidden and may attempt leg attacks with satchel charges.

complications.name: The Recall
complications.text: The Galaxy lifts for the election in 60 hours and the bid cannot be augmented — every other Star is committed to embarkation security. Whatever happens in the fens happens with what was bid.
complications.mechanicalEffect: No reinforcement is available under any condition. At T+60:00 from mission start, all surviving forces must be at the extraction LZ regardless of objective state.

decisionPoints.name: What Is Owed to Looters
decisionPoints.context: Before the force commits, the Star Captain must decide: what honor, if any, is owed to a battalion that ambushed a funeral detail and is now hauling a Bloodnamed warrior to a dissection table? The decision shapes the whole engagement, and it will be read aloud later before the Grand Council.

options.title: Full Batchall
advantages: The forms are kept perfectly: a declared Trial of Possession for the cargo, forces named, ground proposed — no warrior can question the recovery's honor
A declared engagement zone on the causeway prevents the running fight that risks the flatcar
disadvantages: Warning the enemy of the objective invites them to destroy or accelerate the cargo — the dispatch window shows they can advance departure by 11 hours
These are not warriors who answer batchall; the declaration spends surprise and buys probably nothing
options.consequence: The recovery is conducted in full honor against an enemy who will use the warning. The train departs early; the engagement happens at speed, on the causeway, at night.

costs.resource: surprise, bid away by declaration — the dispatch intercepts show the enemy can advance departure by 11 hours
costs.risk: the warned enemy may destroy or accelerate the cargo rather than yield it

options.title: No Quarter Asked
advantages: Corpse-takers merit no declaration — a defensible reading of the honor code that every solahma in the Galaxy would endorse
Surprise at the rail yard before departure is the cleanest tactical solution available
disadvantages: Defensible is not the same as beyond question: a rival Bloodhouse may argue the battalion was never given the chance to hand over a prize it may not have understood it held
A surprise night assault into a rail yard endangers the civilian crew, and the bonus objective with them
options.consequence: The strike goes in silent and total. The recovery is judged afterward not by its forms but by its result — and by what the searchlights catch on gun-camera.

costs.resource: honor: a ruling that is defensible, not unquestionable, judged afterward by result alone
costs.risk: a rival Bloodhouse may argue the looters were never offered the chance to yield; the civilian rail crew and the bonus objective ride on the night assault

options.title: Offer Hegira
advantages: Surround the yard and offer hegira — a free, armed withdrawal — in exchange for the flatcar. It is the rarest honor, offered to a lesser foe, and it is recorded forever
If they accept, you recover the giftake without a shot, and the Remembrance gains a verse no other Clan can claim
disadvantages: Offering hegira to men the Clan calls bandits may look like weakness or mockery; they will probably refuse, and the offer warns them of the attack to come
The encirclement alone eats 8 of your 60 hours and sends the Elementals across the bog in the dark
options.consequence: The offer is made before witnesses. If they accept, this ends without blood. If they refuse, it becomes an assault against an enemy now warned, dug in, and sure of what the cargo is worth.

costs.resource: time: 8 of your 60 recall hours spent on the encirclement, with the Elementals crossing the bog in darkness
costs.risk: hegira offered to a lesser foe and refused warns them of the assault, and may be read as weakness or mockery

entries.event: Force commits — first contact, declaration, or detected approach at the rail yard.
Train can raise steam and begin moving toward the causeway under gun-wagon cover.
Remnant reserve company — light vehicles and infantry — reaches the yard from the fen villages.
Train, once moving, reaches the tunnel mouth at line speed with stops.
Galaxy embarkation closes. The DropShip lifts from the fen-edge LZ.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Two deadlines run at once, and neither can be moved. First, the train reaches the massif at T+19:00 from the moment it starts moving; once the cargo is inside the hardened complex, the small bid force cannot get it back, because digging it out would take a full siege the Loremaster did not bid for. The objective is then lost for good — there is no second attempt. Second, the Galaxy lifts for the election at T+60:00; the recovery force must be at the extraction LZ by then or it is left behind and counted as lost. Losing the giftake into the mountain is the one outcome that cannot be fixed afterward.

opforSketch.composition: Inner Sphere remnant battalion scaled to the band: 1 understrength company of mixed {TARGET_FACTION} BattleMechs (light-medium, worn, Veteran crews), the armored train with 2 gun wagons, 2 platoons of satchel-equipped infantry in the trestles and bog, light vehicles at the yard. No air, no resupply, no line of retreat they intend to use.
opforSketch.behavior: Defense of the train above all; the battalion fights from the bog and the trestle shadows where tonnage cannot follow, masses fire without shame, and attempts to keep the train moving toward the massif under any circumstances. Expect deliberate self-destruction of the cargo before surrender of it.

forks.name: OPERATION HONORED EARTH
forks.trigger: Giftake and remains recovered before the tunnel; force extracted by recall.
forks.consequence: The legacy returns to the sacred ward and the Bloodname Trial proceeds on schedule. The Star Captain's ruling on the looters becomes Clan precedent, cited in councils — and the unit is named escort of honor for the homeward jump.

forks.name: OPERATION MOUNTAIN DEBT
forks.trigger: The train enters the complex with the cargo.
forks.consequence: The debt compounds. A Trial of Possession against the massif itself is petitioned for the invasion's resumption — a deliberate assault on a hardened underground complex, fought by whoever bears the shame of this day, at whatever bid the Loremaster allows.

forks.name: OPERATION ASH VERSE
forks.trigger: The chassis or codex is recovered but the giftake is lost or destroyed.
forks.consequence: The Bloodhouse convenes without its legacy. The unit must carry the codex home and stand witness at the accounting, where the question of the chosen ruling — batchall, silence, or hegira — is asked once per Bloodnamed warrior present.

storyElementSeed: On the fen edge at dusk, an Elemental kneels at the funeral detail's abandoned ground, rights a toppled marker pole with one gauntleted hand, and stands a moment with the helmet sealed before walking on.

phases.name: THE RULING
phases.lead: Before the force commits, the Star Captain decides what is owed to men who looted a funeral detail: a full formal challenge, a silent strike, or hegira — an offered free withdrawal. The decision shapes every hour that follows and will be read aloud before the Grand Council by warriors who were never in the marsh.

dataBlock.The Bid: 1 Star of OmniMechs, 1 Point of Elementals — set by the Loremaster; you cannot add more under any condition
dataBlock.Departure Window: The train leaves within {departureWindow} hours (from intercepts 3 days old, treated as reliable); a warned enemy can move that up by 11 hours
dataBlock.The Recall: Galaxy boarding closes at T+60:00; the DropShip lifts from the marsh-edge LZ with the force aboard or counts it as lost

sidebarKernel.kernel: Rule once and rule whole: a ruling amended at the wire reads, in the record, as a warrior who did not know what was owed until the enemy told him.

phases.name: THE TAKING
phases.lead: The flatcar is taken at the rail yard before steam, or on the causeway at speed — and the ground decides which fight it is. The remnant battalion fights from the bog and the trestle shadows, where tonnage cannot follow and dying well counts as winning.

routes.name: THE CAUSEWAY
routes.desc: The single heavy-rated rail line, 7 meters above the bog on pile-driven trestles, with the armored train and its 2 gun wagons on it.
routes.tradeoff: The only footing for anything over 60 tons — a straight corridor where the train's fixed turrets fire down prepared lanes and the trestle shadows hold satchel infantry.

routes.name: THE FEN CRUST
routes.desc: Frozen peat carrying 60 tons and under at a walk; 1.5 meters of black water beneath.
routes.tradeoff: The flanking approach the train cannot answer — at walking speed, with breakthrough checks, and a winch debt of 3 turns for every machine that misjudges the crust.

dataBlock.Train Composition: Armored locomotive at each end, 2 turreted gun wagons bracketing the flatcar, searchlight mast
dataBlock.Tunnel Clock: T+19:00 from first movement to the tunnel mouth at line speed with stops
dataBlock.Yard Reserve: Remnant reserve company — light vehicles and infantry — arrives from the fen villages at T+1:00

sidebarKernel.kernel: Stopping the train is a geometry problem before it is a gunnery problem: a locomotive killed on a trestle span risks toppling the flatcar 7 meters into the bog, and the objective does not float.

phases.name: THE RETURN
phases.lead: What is recovered is carried home in the manner it deserves. The machine is salvage; the giftake and the warrior are the Clan's, and the difference governs every hand that touches the flatcar.
phases.protocol: Custody of the remains: the senior Elemental Point takes guard the moment the flatcar is secured; the giftake canister and remains travel sealed, witnessed by 2 warriors at every transfer, and are logged to the Loremaster's record by name at the LZ. The codex core is pulled by 1 technician under the same witness. No gun-camera imagery of the remains is taken or kept; the Remembrance does not require photographs.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The giftake is viable if the cockpit has held seal integrity through the winching and the cold — handle the canister transfer as surgery, not as cargo, because in every way that matters to the Clan, it is.

assetDetails.detail: Bloodnamed, twice-honored, dead in the cockpit since the withdrawal ambush. The giftake must be recovered with the remains unviolated; any evidence of Spheroid instrumentation on the body converts the recovery's verse into a grievance the Bloodhouse will pursue for a generation.

9 crew across the 2 locomotives, per the dispatch intercepts — conscripted, unarmed, and riding because the remnant battalion cannot run the line without them. They are no part of any Trial; fire that reaches them is waste wearing the Clan's name, and the bonus objective prices exactly that.

is-kurita.situation.framing: Were this the Dragon's dead, no order would be necessary. The remains of a named warrior carried to an enemy's cutting table is a stain no clock outranks. The Clans, in this one matter, are not alien at all.

merc.objectives.bonus: The rail crew are conscripted civilians per the intercepts. Whatever the cargo is worth to the employer's culture, dead track workers are what ends up in the broadsheets — keep the lanes clean.

title: OPERATION STONE GARDEN
situation: {WORLD} fell in 19 days. {EMPLOYER}'s flag came down at the spaceport, but not in the karst. Your {FORCE_SIZE} is what is left of the planetary garrison, scattered into the limestone country under {EMPLOYER}'s standing stay-behind orders: 3,000 square kilometers of sinkholes, collapsed caverns, and cave systems deep enough to hide a 'Mech's heat signature completely. {EMPLOYER}, speaking through {NPC:quest-giver} on a courier run that reaches you 4 times a year, has confirmed the mission: stay, watch, bleed the occupation, and keep a force alive for the day {EMPLOYER} comes back. Resistance on a {TARGET_FACTION} world starts with the price of defiance. Every officer here knows what the {TARGET_FACTION} did to that city, and so does every civilian who shelters you. The {TARGET_FACTION} keep few troops here — they consider the world beneath serious effort — but their reprisals are the real occupying force. If they trace an operation to a town, they destroy the town. So the standing rule, in every order this command issues: every strike must look like an accident, a bandit raid, or a Clan mistake. Nothing claimed. Nothing proud. This year, {EMPLOYER}'s honor is patience. The terrain runs the whole campaign. Moving faster than 40 kilometers per hour on the surface cracks the karst crust and leaves a scar. A {TARGET_FACTION} spy satellite passes over the district every 4 hours and 17 minutes, and the blind gap between passes is 47 minutes at the cave mouths. Machines move cave to cave inside that gap or they get photographed — and a photograph is a death warrant for whatever town they blame. Current {TARGET_FACTION} forces: 1 garrison Trinary at the spaceport, 1 Star forward at the rail junction, and Elemental sweep teams working the karst on a 9-day cycle. That posture is 2 days old and reliable; the sweep pattern comes from 40 days of logs, so trust its timing loosely. Targets this season: the fuel pipeline feeding the spaceport tank farm, the forward depot, and the rail spur moving {TARGET_FACTION} supplies toward their next wave. One offer you did not ask for: {NPC:smuggler-captain} will sell you ammunition at fair rates, and some of the crates carry ISF seals that are 2 years out of date. Decide what that means before the first crate opens. The hard limit is winter. The karst caves flood when the wet season starts in 9 weeks, so every machine must be moved to the high galleries before the water rises. That move leaves the whole force stuck in place for 6 days, and it cannot wait.

objectives.primary: Cut {TARGET_FACTION} supply through the corridor this season — pipeline flow, depot stocks, or rail tonnage — by a total of 30 percent, with every strike deniable.
objectives.secondary: Keep the force alive and hidden: end the season with at least 80 percent of your combat strength and the cave network undiscovered.
objectives.bonus: Work out the {TARGET_FACTION} launch schedule from the rail traffic you observe, and send it out on the next courier run for {EMPLOYER} to plan around.

complications.name: The Reprisal Precedent
complications.text: Any strike the {TARGET_FACTION} trace to a town, they answer against the town, not the soldiers. Their real weapon is the certainty that they will hit back far harder than the strike itself, and 60,000 civilians in the karst live under that threat.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each strike accrues attribution risk based on method and evidence left; when accumulated attribution crosses the campaign threshold, a named settlement is forfeit and the FAILURE-gated fork triggers immediately, overriding other outcomes.

complications.name: The 47-Minute Gap
complications.text: Satellite passes bracket every surface movement. The blind window at the cave mouths is 47 minutes; a 'Mech that is still in the open at re-acquisition is a photograph, and a photograph is attribution.
complications.mechanicalEffect: All 'Mech-scale surface movement must complete within 47-minute windows occurring every 4 hours 17 minutes. Units caught in the open at window close add a full attribution step.

complications.name: Sweep Cycle
complications.text: {TARGET_FACTION} Elemental teams walk the karst on a 9-day cycle, randomized within sectors. They are thorough, bored, and equipped with seismic listening gear that hears generator plants through 20 meters of limestone.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each cycle, roll one cave sector for a sweep; any sector containing an active power plant or recent vehicle traffic risks discovery. A discovered cave costs its stores and forces relocation during the next satellite gap.

complications.name: Crates With Old Seals
complications.text: {NPC:smuggler-captain}'s resupply is real and the price is fair, which is itself information. ISF seals 2 years stale mean the cargo passed through hands that answer to an agenda this command cannot see from a cave.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Accepting resupply restores ammunition and stores but adds a hidden loyalty thread: one future scenario complication (informant, tracker beacon, or genuine windfall) is rolled secretly when the crates open.

decisionPoints.name: The Season's First Cut
decisionPoints.context: The force can run one major strike before the flood forces the 6-day move to the high galleries. Three targets, each leaving a different trail — and so far the enemy has nothing to trace back to you. {NPC:quest-giver}'s last courier note said only: {EMPLOYER} counts what comes back, not what burns.

options.title: The Pipeline
advantages: Rupturing it at the karst crossing looks like the ground simply sinking — the hardest strike of the three to blame on you
Starving the tank farm slows every {TARGET_FACTION} movement for 3 to 5 weeks, sweep cycle included
disadvantages: It does the least damage of the three, so you will need 2 more strikes to reach the 30 percent goal
Repair crews bring escort Stars into the karst edges for a month
options.consequence: The occupation slows and can prove nothing. The campaign keeps its pace, and you still need everything left on the target list.

costs.resource: one engineered charge set from the cave reserves — the most deniable stock the force holds
costs.risk: repair escorts bring Stars into the karst edges for a month, and you still need 2 more strikes to reach 30 percent

options.title: The Forward Depot
advantages: One strike can take 40 percent of forward stocks in a single fire — the objective in one night
The depot's conscripted labor shift changes at 0300; a strike then minimizes civilian presence to 11 night-watch workers
disadvantages: No accident burns a guarded depot, so they will almost certainly know it was you
The forward Star is 4 minutes away at alert, and your escape window to the caves is a fixed 47 minutes
options.consequence: You hit the season's goal in one stroke, but the enemy is now nearly certain who did it. Their answer lands within days, somewhere.

costs.resource: the season's fire and breaching charges, spent in one night
costs.risk: they will almost certainly trace it to you, and their reprisal doctrine pays that back against a town

options.title: The Rail Spur
advantages: Cumulative track sabotage — culvert collapses, bed subsidence, switch failures — bleeds tonnage 8-12 percent per week and looks like the karst doing what karst does
Distributed small actions train the civilian network in tradecraft the campaign will need for years
disadvantages: Slow: the 30 percent objective arrives in week 7 of 9, with no margin for a failed action
Every civilian cell involved is one more person who can be swept up and questioned
options.consequence: The campaign becomes a long ledger of small deniable cuts. The risk distributes across the network — which is to say, across the people the reprisal precedent prices.

costs.resource: the civilian network — every cell involved is one more person who can be swept up and questioned
costs.risk: the 30 percent objective arrives in week 7 of 9 with no margin for a single failed action

entries.event: Strike detected — alarm at the target or anomaly flagged in {TARGET_FACTION} telemetry.
Forward Star at the rail junction moves at alert speed toward the strike site.
Aerospace point overflies from the spaceport strip; thermal sweep of approach routes begins.
Satellite re-acquisition over the karst. Anything in the open is photographed.
Wet season begins; cave flooding starts in the lower galleries.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Strike elements must be underground before satellite re-acquisition at T+0:47 — the gap does not stretch. And the entire force must complete the 6-day relocation to the high galleries before wet season at week 9; a force caught mid-move by a sweep cycle is a force found.

opforSketch.composition: Occupation force scaled to the band: 1 second-line Trinary at the spaceport, 1 forward Star (mixed OmniMechs, alert posture) at the rail junction, Elemental sweep teams of 1-2 Points in the karst, 1 aerospace point on strip alert, and the surveillance satellite. Reinforcement above this level requires {TARGET_FACTION} to admit a resistance exists, which they will not do until the evidence is public.
opforSketch.behavior: Contempt at the strategic level, precision at the tactical: sweeps are methodical, responses to confirmed contact are fast and overwhelming, and reprisal targeting is bureaucratic — a settlement is selected, announced, and made an example, exactly once per proven incident.

forks.name: OPERATION KARST CHORUS
forks.trigger: Season objective met, force preserved, attribution below threshold.
forks.consequence: The courier circuit returns with {EMPLOYER} tasking: the network's intelligence has been graded strategic, and the next season's mission adds target designation for an off-world strike — guiding {EMPLOYER}'s hand from inside the cage.

forks.name: OPERATION HOLLOW BELL
forks.trigger: Attribution crosses threshold; a settlement is named for reprisal.
forks.consequence: The {TARGET_FACTION} announce the reprisal 72 hours ahead, because terror needs an audience. The force has to evacuate a town of {settlementPopulation} through the karst, under the satellite — and do it without proving, by the rescue itself, that the resistance they are punishing is real.

forks.name: OPERATION DRY CISTERN
forks.trigger: A cave sector is discovered or the smuggler thread resolves against the force.
forks.consequence: The network is partially rolled up. Survivors consolidate in the flood-margin galleries with 60 percent of stores lost, and the season's remaining operations are conducted by a force that now knows it is being hunted by name.

storyElementSeed: In a cave gallery lit by two work lamps, a pilot brushes condensation off a tarped 'Mech's foot and re-checks the wheel chocks while, farther in, the cooking fire is being fed only wood dry enough to make no smoke.

phases.name: THE BEDDING
phases.lead: The campaign is won or lost in posture before a single charge is laid: machines bedded in the deep galleries, generators silenced against seismic ears, movement disciplined to the satellite's arithmetic. Patience is {EMPLOYER}'s honor this year, and patience has procedures.

dataBlock.Satellite Period: 4 hours 17 minutes per pass; usable blind gap at the cave mouths: 47 minutes
dataBlock.Sweep Cycle: {TARGET_FACTION} Elemental teams, 9-day cycle, randomized within sectors, seismic gear hears generators through 20 meters of limestone
dataBlock.Surface Speed Limit: 40 kilometers per hour — above it, karst crust shatters and the scar is a photograph waiting for the next pass
dataBlock.Courier Circuit: 4 contacts per year; the next departure carries whatever the bonus objective has assembled

phases.protocol: Movement order: no 'Mech leaves a cave mouth except inside a declared 47-minute window, logged against the pass schedule by the watch officer; generator hours rotate between sectors so no gallery runs power 2 sweep-cycles in a row; nothing written leaves the caves, and the courier's material is memorized or microfilmed, never both.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The sweep pattern is built from 40 days of logs at MEDIUM confidence — trust the cycle's length, never its order, and move the watch posts the day any sweep arrives early.

phases.name: THE CUT
phases.lead: One major strike before the flood move, chosen against the attribution ledger as much as the target list. The courier's note stands as the season's whole doctrine: {EMPLOYER} counts what returns, not what burns.

dataBlock.Attribution Risk: Starts at zero; reaches the limit at {attributionThreshold} steps, and crossing it costs a town under their reprisal doctrine
dataBlock.Egress Arithmetic: Forward Star at the rail junction: 4 minutes at alert; satellite re-acquisition: T+0:47, fixed
dataBlock.Target Board: Pipeline (deniable, slow), forward depot (decisive, attributable), rail spur (cumulative, distributed)

sidebarKernel.kernel: Plan every strike twice — once as the operation, once as the story {TARGET_FACTION} will reconstruct from its residue — and cancel any strike whose second version has a town's name in it.

phases.name: THE RELOCATION
phases.lead: At week 9 the water rises and the entire force moves to the high galleries: 6 days immobile, machines on cribbing, stores on backs, the campaign's whole existence in transit under the sweep cycle. Nothing this season is allowed to schedule against those 6 days.

dataBlock.Move Duration: 6 days, force immobile throughout; the move cannot wait and cannot be split
dataBlock.Flood Onset: Wet season begins week 9; lower galleries flood first
dataBlock.Exposure: A force caught mid-move by a sweep is a force found — the relocation is the campaign's single largest attribution risk

sidebarKernel.kernel: Stage the high galleries now: rations, dry wood, and cribbing placed before week 7, because in week 9 every hand is under a 'Mech and the satellite does not observe a harvest holiday.

assetDetails.detail: The resupply offer is real, the rates are tolerable, and the ISF seals on the manifest crates are 2 years out of date — which means the cargo passed through hands that answer to an agenda invisible from a cave. Decide what the seals mean before the first crate opens; the decision cannot be unmade after.

Speaks for {EMPLOYER} on a courier circuit that arrives 4 times a year and cannot be queried between contacts. Orders are standing doctrine, not conversation — any situation the last courier did not anticipate is the commander's alone until the next one grounds.

merc.situation.framing: No contract covers this. Stay-behind work is what happens when the employer's flag leaves orbit faster than the employees — read the force-preservation objective as the only clause still paying.

clan.opforSketch.behavior: The bandits in the stones are beneath the honor of declaration. They will be swept as vermin are swept, and the dwellings that shelter them are part of the infestation. This is not war. War is owed to warriors.

forceStartingMechs.unit: operational BattleMechs in the dispersal force

resourceGates.lackingText: Cave stores cannot cover the strike load: {NPC:smuggler-captain} prices the munitions at 90,000 C-bills in trade goods — delivered in crates whose ISF seals are 2 years out of date.

title: OPERATION PATIENT TIDE
situation: {WORLD} is not a raid target. It is a future home, though the {TARGET_FACTION} do not yet know it will be ours. The Khans have marked this world for the Clan to settle — its shipyards, its arcologies, its winters that feel right — and you take a home differently than you take a trophy. The Galaxy Commander's order is plain: what we break here, we repair here, as its new residents. Bid and fight with that in mind. The {TARGET_FACTION} answered our batchall with defiance, which was expected and is respected. Their defense of the capital sits on the mudflats: 14 kilometers of tidal plain in front of the arcology district, flooding to 2.2 meters on a 5-hour-40-minute cycle. At low water the flats carry any weight on a hard sand crust for 4 hours and 10 minutes; then the tide comes back faster than a damaged 'Mech can crawl clear. The only route open at all tides is the forest corridor to the north — 9 kilometers of planted pine on firm ground, with every {TARGET_FACTION} artillery battery already ranged in on it. That fire plan comes from a prisoner questioned 5 days ago, so treat it as likely, not certain. The defenders are {defenderRegiments} regiments of mixed regulars and militia with conscript fill under {NPC:opfor-commander}, dug in with their backs to their own homes; that intelligence is 5 days old and reliable. These are not some lesser Clan's cannon fodder. They are heirs of the pilot who rammed an ilKhan out of the sky over a neighboring world, and since that day their pilots have learned to make their deaths count. Expect ramming. Expect demolition charges in buildings their own grandparents built. Expect, in the same hour, white flags from conscript companies whose officers are already dead — and honor every one, because this world will remember its first week under us for a century. Two rules bind the assault from above. First: the ComStar compound and its HPG relay sit inside the arcology district and are off-limits under the Khans' agreement. No fire plan touches its map square, no matter what shelters behind it. Second: the bid. The Galaxy Commander has bid away all naval bombardment and heavy artillery — you do not soften a home from orbit — and the Star Colonels have set the ground force at {bidClusters} Clusters with Elemental support and matching aerospace, nothing held back that was not named. The assault clock is the tide table. You must take the arcology power district before tide cycle 4 closes at T+22:40. Miss it and the flats reset, the garrison rebuilds its line, and this clean assault becomes a 9-day street-by-street grind through the city we mean to live in, quiaff?

objectives.primary: Seize the arcology power district intact before tide cycle 4 closes at T+22:40.
objectives.secondary: Break the garrison's organized resistance on the line while accepting every surrender offered and processing it by Clan law.
objectives.bonus: Take the yard-control facilities undamaged — the infrastructure of the home, not the spoils of the trophy.

complications.name: The Tide Table
complications.text: The flats open for 4 hours 10 minutes per cycle and drown to 2.2 meters between. An assault echelon that mistimes its crossing fights the second half of its battle in rising water, and a disabled machine on the flats is a lost machine, crew and all, unless pulled before the water wins.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Flats hexes are passable to all units during the low-water window and become depth-2 water on a fixed turn schedule thereafter. Immobilized units in flooding hexes must be towed out within the schedule or are eliminated; crews may eject.

complications.name: Pre-Registered Forest
complications.text: The forest corridor is the only all-tide approach and the garrison has had a year to register its batteries on every firebreak and bend. The trees do not hide anything; they merely decide where the wreckage stacks.
complications.mechanicalEffect: All hexes in the corridor are pre-registered: defending artillery fires without spotting penalty there, every turn, until counter-battery silences each named battery position.

complications.name: Endings That Mean Something
complications.text: {TARGET_FACTION} aerospace and armor crews attempt ramming and point-blank demolition when crippled. Since that day, this is not desperation; it is doctrine with a martyr's name on it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any crippled defender unit in contact range may attempt a ramming or self-destruction attack instead of withdrawing or surrendering; roll per unit at the moment it becomes crippled.

complications.name: Surrenders in Mid-Battle
complications.text: Conscript companies break and yield in formed bodies, in the open, mid-engagement, while their neighbors fight on. Each acceptance is law, and each costs combat power to escort and process while the tide clock runs.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each accepted surrender removes one defending unit from play and commits one attacking unit (or Elemental Point) to escort duty for 2 turns. Refusing or firing on a surrender forces the COMPROMISED gate.

decisionPoints.name: The Garrison's Petition
decisionPoints.context: At T+9:00, with the line bending, {NPC:opfor-commander} transmits in the open: a request for hegira — free withdrawal under arms for the garrison's remnant, the civil government, and the military academy's cadets, in exchange for the city unmined and the power district intact. The transmission is addressed correctly, in passable Clan form. Someone over there has been studying. The reply belongs to the assault commander, and the tide does not pause for deliberation.

options.title: Grant Hegira
advantages: The city, the power district, and the yards come over intact — the home undamaged, the primary and bonus objectives effectively conceded
Granting the first hegira of the invasion to a worthy foe is a verse the Remembrance will keep, and a precedent that makes the next world's garrison likelier to ask than to burn
disadvantages: The garrison's remnant — and a full class of academy cadets — withdraws to fight the Clan again on the next world, trained now by this defeat
Warriors who bid for glory on the flats are paid in an administrative occupation; the bidding chiefs will remember who ended their Trial with paperwork
options.consequence: The withdrawal is honored and watched to the horizon. {WORLD} is taken whole, and every soldier permitted to leave is a future engagement deferred at interest.

costs.resource: the bid's glory — warriors who bid for the flats are paid in an administrative occupation, and the bidding chiefs will remember
costs.risk: the garrison remnant and a full academy class withdraw to fight the Clan again, trained by this defeat

options.title: Demand Surrender Instead
advantages: An unconditional surrender turns the garrison into the Clan's own future — abtakha, captives absorbed into the Clan as laborers and eventually kin; a home needs people more than prisoners
No armed force withdraws to reinforce the next defensive line in the corridor
disadvantages: The counter-offer insults a foe who asked correctly; the probable answer is demolition charges in the power district and a last stand among the homes
Negotiation consumes the remainder of tide cycle 3 — if it fails, the assault resumes with one window left
options.consequence: The reply is honor of a harder kind. If they yield, the Clan gains a population; if they refuse, the assault must take by storm, in one tide, what the petition offered for nothing.

costs.resource: time: the remainder of tide cycle 3 consumed by negotiation — one assault window left if it fails
costs.risk: the counter-offer insults a foe who asked correctly; the probable answer is demolition charges in the power district

options.title: Press the Assault
advantages: No pause, no risk of a feint: the line is bending now and tide cycle 3 favors the attack for 2 more hours
The bidding chiefs are answered — the Trial is completed as bid, by arms, and no one before the Grand Council can call the victory negotiated
disadvantages: Refusing a correctly made petition without answer is within the law and beneath the Clan's better story of itself — this world will remember it
A garrison denied hegira fights like those pilots flew; expect the power district wired before the flats clear
options.consequence: The petition goes unanswered and the assault rolls through it. Whatever is taken is taken by strength alone, priced accordingly, and remembered accordingly — on both sides.

costs.resource: honor: a correctly made petition refused without answer — within the law, beneath the Clan's better story of itself
costs.risk: a garrison denied hegira fights like those pilots flew; expect the power district wired before the flats clear

entries.event: First assault echelon crosses the flats line at low water; tide cycle 1 opens.
Tide cycle 1 closes; the flats drown. Forces ashore hold the bridgehead unsupported until cycle 2.
Projected garrison petition window; the line bends or breaks by this hour.
Tide cycle 4 opens — the final crossing window for the power district push.
Tide cycle 4 closes. The assault has succeeded by now or it has become a siege.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The power district falls before T+22:40 or the operation converts to a 9-day urban reduction of the city the Clan intends to inhabit — a failure measured not in honor but in everything the word home was bid to mean.

opforSketch.composition: Planetary defense scaled to the band: {defenderRegiments} regiments of {TARGET_FACTION} regulars and militia (Regular quality with Veteran cadre, conscript fill at 20-30 percent), dug-in armor on the arcology line, tube artillery registered on the forest corridor, and a reduced aerospace wing that has already chosen how it wishes to be remembered.
opforSketch.behavior: Static defense anchored on the tide table, artillery doctrine in the forest, counterattacks timed to flood windows. Crippled units seek endings of consequence; intact conscript formations seek endings of survival. The commander husbands the regulars for the arcology line and will trade the militia for time.

forks.name: OPERATION HEARTH RIGHT
forks.trigger: Power district taken intact within the tide deadline.
forks.consequence: The Clan's claim on {WORLD} becomes administration within a season. The unit is granted first-settlement honors — and tasked with the occupation's first true test: integrating {abtakhaCount} prisoners and a sullen arcology population into a Clan world without becoming tyrants.

forks.name: OPERATION LONG WINTER
forks.trigger: Tide cycle 4 closes with the power district untaken or destroyed.
forks.consequence: The siege begins. Nine days of street reduction through a wired city, with the Khans' attention acquired and the bid's honor spent. The follow-on mission is the assault's own wreckage: take by attrition what was bid to be taken by skill.

forks.name: OPERATION COLD ACCOUNT
forks.trigger: A surrender was refused or fired upon, or the ComStar grid square was struck.
forks.consequence: The violation travels — to the Khans, to ComStar's adepts, to the {TARGET_FACTION} communes who now know what the new neighbors do to white flags. The occupation inherits an insurgency before it inherits a city, and the responsible commander answers a summons to a circle of a different kind.

storyElementSeed: On the re-hardening flats between tides, a recovery crew works chain hooks under a mired 'Mech's knee while a kilometer out the water stands in a gray line, neither advancing nor pretending it will wait.

phases.name: THE CROSSING
phases.lead: Tide cycle 1 opens and the first echelon crosses 14 kilometers of hard sand against the clock that commands both armies. A home is not softened from orbit; it is walked into, at low water, by warriors who have read the tide table.

routes.name: THE MUDFLATS
routes.desc: 14 kilometers of tidal plain, hard crust carrying any tonnage for 4 hours 10 minutes per cycle, flooding to 2.2 meters between.
routes.tradeoff: The broad front and the fast approach — purchased against a clock that drowns the slow, the damaged, and the mistimed without regard for honor.

routes.name: THE FOREST CORRIDOR
routes.desc: 9 kilometers of planted pine on firm ground, the only route open at all tides.
routes.tradeoff: No tide clock — but every firebreak and bend is already ranged in by every battery the garrison owns, per a prisoner questioned 5 days ago (likely, not certain).

dataBlock.Tide Cycle: 5 hours 40 minutes full cycle; low-water window 4 hours 10 minutes; flood depth 2.2 meters
dataBlock.Bridgehead Gap: Forces ashore at cycle close hold unsupported until the next window opens
dataBlock.Recovery Rule: A disabled machine on the flats is pulled before the water wins or it is lost with its crew

sidebarKernel.kernel: The tide table is the operation's true commander: every echelon, every tow line, and every casualty plan is timed from the water, and the water has never granted hegira to anyone.

phases.name: THE LINE
phases.lead: The line is held by heirs of that martyr who fight in front of their own homes, and the same hour will bring ramming attacks and white flags from conscript companies whose officers are dead. Every surrender is honored and processed by Clan law; this world will remember its first week of us for a century.
phases.protocol: Surrender processing: each accepted formation is escorted by 1 attacking unit or Elemental Point for 2 turns to the rear collection line, logged by formation and hour, weapons grounded and untouched until the collection details arrive. The ComStar compound's grid square is inviolate under the Khans' arrangement: no fire plan touches it, whatever displaces behind it, and every targeting log is retained for the adepts' inspection.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Prisoner and casualty flows arrive together and double at every surrender — stage the processing line for {abtakhaCount} before cycle 2, because a home's first census must not begin with the wounded lying unsorted on a beach.

phases.name: THE PETITION
phases.lead: At T+9:00 the garrison commander transmits in the open, in passable Clan form, asking hegira. Someone over there has been studying; the reply belongs to the assault commander, and the tide does not pause for deliberation.

dataBlock.Petition Terms: Free withdrawal under arms for the garrison remnant, civil government, and academy cadets, against the city unmined and the power district intact
dataBlock.Negotiation Cost: A counter-offer consumes the remainder of tide cycle 3 — one assault window remains if it fails
dataBlock.Form: The transmission is correctly addressed; the law permits grant, counter-demand, or silence, and each is answered for afterward

sidebarKernel.kernel: Weigh the petition as the founding document of the occupation it precedes: whichever answer is given, it will be quoted on this world longer than any battle honor won on the flats.

phases.name: THE POWER DISTRICT
phases.lead: Tide cycle 4 opens at T+17:00 and closes at T+22:40, and inside that window the power district is taken intact or the operation becomes a 9-day reduction of the city the Clan intends to inhabit. What is broken here is repaired here, by residents.

dataBlock.Final Window: T+17:00 to T+22:40 — the last crossing the assault schedule recognizes
dataBlock.Intact Requirement: The district's generation halls are the objective in working order; demolition charges are the probable answer to a refused petition
dataBlock.After the Window: The flats reset, the garrison re-seats its line, and the deliberate assault becomes siege

sidebarKernel.kernel: Send the breach teams in with the disarming kits, not behind them — a generation hall taken 11 minutes after its charges fire is a trophy, and this Clan did not cross the void for trophies.

is-davion.situation.defenderNote: From the garrison's map table: the flats buy 4-hour battles, the forest costs them batteries, and the only question that matters is whether the invader's patience outlasts the tide table. Everything AFFC observers learn here gets paid for in the defenders' blood first.

comstar.complications[3].text: The compound's inviolability is the single thread of the Khans' arrangement that touches ground on {WORLD}. Both armies will test whether the other believes in it; the Order's task is to make belief cheaper than the alternative.

title: OPERATION ASH CURTAIN
situation: {WORLD} is an open wound this Galaxy still carries. In the great rift, a single Inner Sphere trap wiped out an entire {EMPLOYER} Guards Cluster — not beaten, wiped out — with buried explosives set by a commander who fought like a surveyor with a map, not a warrior in a circle. The Inner Sphere still holds the world, garrisoned by {defenderBattalions} battalions of {TARGET_FACTION} troops proud of the one victory of its kind they own. That garrison estimate is 8 days old and likely; their patrol schedule was confirmed by an aerospace pass 2 days ago and is reliable. The Khan wants the world back. The Loremaster wants something harder: it must be won in a way that heals the shame, not just avenges it. The batchall has been sent, and {NPC:opfor-commander} answered with a politeness that is itself an insult — he thanked the Clan for warning him. On {WORLD} the ground decides everything, because the wind owns the ground. Between the landing zones and the capital lies the dust plain: 70 kilometers of hardpan swept by the diabolis — rolling dust storms that cut sight and sensors to between 90 and 300 meters, ground all aerospace below 4,000 meters, and scour exposed seals on a 6-hour cycle. The storm season is forecast to hold for {stormWindowHours} more hours, then break clear for 5 days; that forecast is reliable, drawn from the Clan's own occupation-era records. Inside the storm you cannot keep zellbrigen — the one-on-one dueling code — because no warrior can call out a target the dust has not yet shown at 200 meters. The enemy knows it, and since the rift their doctrine is massed short-range fire from hidden dug-in nests: anonymous, dishonorable, and effective. There are two other routes. The great rift itself is 40 kilometers of canyon highway through the mountains — fast, sheltered from the dust, and the exact ground where the Guards died. Engineering puts it at 60 percent that the garrison has mined it again, but that is a low-confidence guess from watching cargo move. Or the salt flats south of the mountains: open, storm-free, unmined, undefended — but 31 hours longer, which burns the storm window and lands the assault on open ground under the enemy's full sensors. The garrison's DropShips sit fueled at the capital field. When the storm breaks, the enemy can lift off — and a Trial that ends with the enemy escaping in good order wins back the world but not the honor. By the Khan's direct order, the rebuilt {EMPLOYER} Guards Cluster is in the bid. They are not here to take part. They are here to be seen winning, quiaff?

objectives.primary: Take the capital and its DropShip field before the storm break at {stormWindowHours} hours grounds the garrison's option to extract.
objectives.secondary: Destroy or compel the surrender of the garrison's BattleMech battalions — the world returned with its defenders accounted for, not escaped.
objectives.bonus: The reconstituted {EMPLOYER} Guards take a named, witnessed objective — gate, field, or garrison standard — with their own bid and no assistance.

complications.name: The Diabolis
complications.text: Dust vortices walk the dust plain on no schedule a fire plan can use. Sensor and visual range falls to 90-300 meters inside a curtain, aerospace is grounded below 4,000 meters, and a formation that loses cohesion in the dust re-forms by luck or not at all.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On the plain, roll each turn for curtain coverage by sector: affected hexes cap all detection at {curtainVisibility} meters, prohibit indirect fire without a same-sector spotter, and ground all air support. Formations moving faster than walking speed in a curtain risk separation.

complications.name: The Seeded Rift
complications.text: Engineering puts it at 60 percent that the canyon is mined again, based on 8-day-old cargo sightings and a memory of the rift no one needs reminding of. Sweeping all 40 kilometers takes 9 hours; sweeping only the chokepoints takes 3 hours but leaves the rest unchecked.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the rift axis is chosen, the seeding probability resolves secretly at mission start. Unswept canyon hexes may contain command-detonated fields; a triggered field attacks every unit in a 3-hex column section simultaneously.

complications.name: Nests in the Dust
complications.text: The garrison's anti-Clan doctrine is hull-down anonymity: dug-in 'Mechs and armor holding fire to 200 meters, volleying massed autocannon and missiles, displacing under the curtain to the next nest. No declarations, no duels, no shame in their book at all.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Defender nests deploy hidden on the plain and in the approaches; each fires as a massed volley on first reveal. Zellbrigen cannot be maintained inside curtain sectors — honor outcomes are scored only on engagements outside the dust.

complications.name: Fueled DropShips
complications.text: The garrison's lift sits ready at the capital field. The moment the storm breaks, extraction is a 4-hour operation under their remaining air cover. Every hour of assault delay is an hour of their countdown banked.
complications.mechanicalEffect: At storm break, a 4-hour evacuation clock starts: each elapsed hour thereafter removes one defending battalion (and its accounting toward the secondary objective) from the world.

decisionPoints.name: The Axis of the Wound
decisionPoints.context: Three axes to the capital, and the choice is not tactical only — every warrior of {EMPLOYER} from the Khan down will read it as the Clan's answer to the rift. The bidding chiefs are split. The storm window is not.

options.title: Through the rift
advantages: The fastest axis by 14 hours, sheltered from the diabolis, with the assault arriving inside the storm window at full strength
Retaking the exact ground of the humiliation, swept and conquered, closes the wound in the only language the Remembrance respects
disadvantages: A 60 percent seeding assessment at LOW confidence is a coin flipped over a mass grave
The garrison wants the rift chosen — whatever waits there was prepared with this exact pride in mind
options.consequence: The canyon is swept at the chokepoints and forced. The wound closes or reopens in the same 40 kilometers, before witnesses, with the {EMPLOYER} Guards in the column.

costs.resource: sweep time: 3 hours at the chokepoints against 9 for the full canyon — the axis's 14-hour advantage is spent in proportion to certainty
costs.risk: a 60 percent seeding assessment at LOW confidence, resolved over the {EMPLOYER} Guards' grave, before witnesses

options.title: Into the Curtains
advantages: The storm blinds the enemy's sensors and grounds their aircraft as fully as it does the Clan's — and at 200 meters, Clan guns and Clan armor win the close-range fight
No mines, no canyon, no script: the route the garrison can least prepare for
disadvantages: Zellbrigen dissolves in the dust — the Trial becomes anonymous mass combat, exactly the warfare the Clans crossed the void to end
Navigation losses, seal abrasion, and formation separation tax the assault before the first nest fires
options.consequence: The assault advances inside the diabolis, trading honor's forms for the storm's cover. Victory will be real and unbeautiful, and the Loremaster's record will say both.

costs.resource: honor: zellbrigen dissolves in the dust — the Trial fought as anonymous mass combat; seal abrasion taxes every machine on the 6-hour cycle
costs.risk: navigation losses and formation separation on the plain before the first nest fires; contact at the capital no earlier than T+26:00

options.title: The Salt Flank
advantages: Unmined, stormless, undefended ground — the approach itself is nearly free of risk
Full sensor and air superiority once clear of the storm shadow: the Clan fights its preferred battle in the open
disadvantages: 31 additional hours spends the storm window; the assault arrives as the garrison's evacuation clock starts running
The axis concedes that the Clan went around — around the rift, around the dust, around the wound. The enemy's broadcasts will say so within the day
options.consequence: The approach is clean and the deadline is mortgaged. The assault opens against a garrison free to choose between a parting fight and a punctual extraction.

costs.resource: time: 31 additional hours — the storm window mortgaged in transit, with contact at T+43:00
costs.risk: the assault opens as the garrison's 4-hour lift clock runs, and the enemy's broadcasts will say the Clan went around the wound

entries.event: Landing zones secured at the storm's edge; the garrison's sensor net registers the descent regardless of dust.
Garrison covering forces displace to forward nests; demolition and mine watch teams man the rift overlooks.
Earliest assault contact at the capital's outer line via the rift axis; T+26:00 via the Plain; T+43:00 via the salt flats.
Forecast storm break. Garrison evacuation option opens; their 4-hour lift clock can start.
First garrison battalion can be off-world.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The capital field must be taken before the storm breaks at T+{stormWindowHours}:00. If it has not fallen by then, the garrison's fueled DropShips begin lifting off — one enemy battalion per hour — and there is nothing the Clan can do about it from whatever ground its chosen axis reached. Every battalion that escapes is one the secondary objective can no longer account for, and an enemy that gets away in good order means the operation has not achieved its purpose: the world is returned, but the defenders who must be beaten or captured are simply gone.

opforSketch.composition: {TARGET_FACTION} garrison scaled to the band: {defenderBattalions} BattleMech battalions (Regular-Veteran, anti-Clan doctrine conversions), supporting armor in hull-down nests, conventional air held for the storm break, engineer units with command-detonated fields, and fueled DropShip lift at the capital. Quality concentrated in 1 veteran battalion blooded in the original fighting here.
opforSketch.behavior: Defense by denial and anonymity: hidden nests, massed volleys at minimum range, displacement under dust cover, no formal engagement accepted anywhere. The commander fights the clock, not the Clan — every action is priced against the evacuation option, and the rift is held cheap precisely because they hope it will be chosen.

forks.name: OPERATION CLOSED CIRCLE
forks.trigger: the capital taken inside the storm window with the garrison accounted for.
forks.consequence: The wound is closed and the Remembrance gains its verse — with the {EMPLOYER} Guards' part scored separately, as the Khan intended. The Galaxy rolls forward on the wave schedule with its reputation repaired and every rival Clan's eyes on what it does next.

forks.name: OPERATION GASH ECHO
forks.trigger: The assault is broken, or the garrison extracts in good order.
forks.consequence: {WORLD} is held or half-held and the wound is now a legend with a sequel. The Khan strips the bidding chiefs' honors, and the follow-on assault is fought by warriors bidding double against each other for the right to redeem what this one spent.

forks.name: OPERATION DUST LEDGER
forks.trigger: the capital taken after storm break, with garrison elements escaped.
forks.consequence: The world is returned; the defenders' cadre is not. The escaped battalions reappear behind the truce line as the Inner Sphere's anti-Clan instructors, and the Clan's next three worlds are defended by students of this exact battle.

storyElementSeed: At the storm's edge, a warrior runs a gloved thumb along the fresh abrasion grooves in a 'Mech's shin armor, checks the seal tape on the knee actuator a second time, and says nothing to the technician who already knows.

phases.name: THE BID AND THE AXIS
phases.lead: The bidding chiefs are split and the storm window is not. The axis chosen will be read from the Khan down as the Clan's answer to the rift — the decision is strategic, ceremonial, and meteorological in the same breath, and it is made once.

routes.name: THE RIFT
routes.desc: 40 kilometers of canyon highway through the mountains: the fastest route by 14 hours, sheltered from the diabolis — and the exact ground where the {EMPLOYER} Guards died.
routes.tradeoff: Sweeping the chokepoints takes 3 hours, the full canyon 9; the 60 percent chance it is mined again is only a low-confidence guess, and you are betting lives on it.

routes.name: THE DUST PLAIN
routes.desc: 70 kilometers of hardpan walked by the diabolis, sensor and visual range 90 to 300 meters inside a curtain, all aerospace grounded below 4,000 meters.
routes.tradeoff: The storm blinds the enemy net as thoroughly as the Clan's own — and zellbrigen dissolves in dust that reveals no target to declare.

routes.name: THE SALT FLANK
routes.desc: The salt flats south of the mountains: open, stormless, unmined, undefended.
routes.tradeoff: 31 additional hours that mortgage the storm window — and an axis that concedes, on every enemy broadcast, that the Clan went around the wound.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Bid the axis, not only the force: each road to the capital carries its own honor price, and the Khan's word has already placed the {EMPLOYER} Guards in the column wherever it marches.

phases.name: THE ADVANCE
phases.lead: Whatever axis was chosen, the advance is a race against the forecast: contact at the capital's outer line at T+12:00 by the rift, T+26:00 by the Plain, T+43:00 by the salt. The garrison fights the clock, not the Clan, and holds the rift cheap precisely because it hopes the rift is chosen.

dataBlock.Storm Window: {stormWindowHours} hours until the forecast break, then 5 clear days — a reliable forecast, from the Clan's own occupation-era records
dataBlock.Abrasion Cycle: Exposed seals scour on a 6-hour cycle inside the storm; seal checks are a formation halt, 20 minutes per Star
dataBlock.Nest Doctrine: Hull-down volleys at 200 meters, displacement under the curtain — anonymous, undeclarable, effective

phases.protocol: Recognition inside the curtains: friendly machines carry a 3-pulse transponder cadence on the Trial frequency, repeated at 90-second intervals; any contact at under 300 meters without the cadence is engaged without declaration, by standing order — the dust has already taken the declarations away, and fratricide is the only dishonor left to add.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The 6-hour abrasion cycle is not advisory: a knee seal that misses 2 checks fails in the third curtain, and a 'Mech down for seal failure on the Plain is recovered at the storm's convenience, not ours.

phases.name: THE CAPITAL FIELD
phases.lead: The field is taken before the storm break or the secondary objective begins lifting off the world at a battalion every hour while the Clan watches. The {EMPLOYER} Guards take their named objective with their own bid and no assistance — they are not here to participate; they are here to be seen winning.

dataBlock.Evacuation Clock: 4 hours from storm break to first garrison battalion off-world; 1 additional battalion per hour after
dataBlock.Fueled Lift: Garrison DropShips stand ready at the field under their remaining air cover
dataBlock.Witnessed Objective: Gate, field, or garrison standard — named in the bid, taken before witnesses, scored separately as the Khan intended

sidebarKernel.kernel: Watch the field's fuel lines, not its gates. A garrison disconnecting and capping its DropShip fuel hoses has chosen to stand and fight; one that leaves them hooked up is already counting down to the storm break and a fast escape.

assetDetails.detail: In the bid by the Khan's explicit word, carrying the rift on every roster. Their warriors will overbid and overreach to erase it; assign their named objective where boldness is an asset and a second demolition trap is not, and place witnesses where the Remembrance needs them — the Khan requires them seen winning, not avenged twice.

is-davion.situation.defenderNote: Garrison side of the hill: you beat them here once with geology and patience, they have announced they are coming back, and the only winning move is to make them buy every axis while the DropShips stay fueled. Pride is their supply line. Cut it.

merc.opforSketch.behavior: Translation for professionals: the defenders fight like a unit that read the Clan rulebook and burned it. Hull-down, massed fire, no radio chatter, and a paid-up extraction plan. It is the most rational army on the planet and it is not yours.

curtainVisibility.unit: meters of detection inside a dust curtain
